summary: Robinhood expanded its Agentic Trading feature to include crypto on July 10, 2026, allowing eligible US customers among its roughly 27.5 million users to connect third-party AI agents for automated 24/7 digital asset trading within user-defined safety guardrails.

title: Helsing mass-produces AI-powered war drones for Ukraine
summary: The New York Times revealed Helsing SE's secret factory producing mass quantities of inexpensive AI-powered drones for Ukraine's war effort, marking a major shift in AI-driven military hardware at scale.

title: FuriosaAI RNGD inference chip goes live in Europe at Equinix Lisbon
summary: South Korean AI chip startup FuriosaAI activated its RNGD inference accelerator servers at Equinix's LS2 colocation facility in Lisbon, Portugal, the company's first confirmed commercial production deployment on European soil.

title: China Blocks Meta's Manus AI Deal; Tencent in Talks for $2B Buyback
summary: Beijing's NDRC ordered Meta's $2 billion acquisition of agentic AI firm Manus reversed, using China's Foreign Investment Security Review mechanism and citing the Chinese origin of the technology despite Manus's Singapore corporate structure. Tencent, ZhenFund, and HSG are in talks to reacquire Manus at the same $2 billion valuation, with Tencent as the largest single but minority stakeholder; no deal has been signed.

title: EDPS and EDPB Warn AI Hiring Tools Have Violated GDPR Art. 22 Since 2018
summary: At a July 9 conference co-hosted by the EDPS and EDPB at the European Parliament, regulators stated that AI candidate screening tools lacking genuine human review have been in violation of GDPR Article 22 since it took effect in May 2018, and that the Digital Omnibus extension of the EU AI Act deadline to December 2027 provides no safe harbour under existing data protection law.

title: San Francisco Moves to Fine AV Firms for Emergency Blockages
summary: San Francisco Supervisor Connie Chan is working with the city attorney to draft legislation that would create a cost recovery fee for autonomous vehicle companies when their vehicles cause false emergency reports or impede emergency responses. The proposed measure, which targets companies including Waymo, is expected to be presented to the full Board of Supervisors in the coming months.

title: Record industry proposes voluntary AI-generated music labelling system
summary: The RIAA, the Grammys, SAG-AFTRA, and other music organizations jointly proposed a voluntary labelling system to disclose AI use in recordings, using distinct digital markers for AI-generated and AI-assisted tracks. It is unclear when or if streaming services will implement the labels.

title: Apple sues OpenAI over alleged AI trade secret theft
summary: Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, its Chief Hardware Officer Tang Tan, and former Apple employee Chang Liu, alleging trade secret misappropriation and breach of contract. Apple claims OpenAI's senior leadership directed a pattern of theft to benefit its nascent hardware business, and is seeking to bar OpenAI from using or disclosing its confidential information.

title: Meta Suspends Instagram AI Image Remix Feature After Backlash
summary: Meta pulled its Muse Image Instagram feature within days of launch after Hollywood guilds including SAG-AFTRA and CAA objected to the tool's ability to generate AI images incorporating other users' public Instagram photos without consent.

title: Colorado replaces 2024 AI law with narrower SB 26-189
summary: Colorado Governor Jared Polis signed Senate Bill 26-189 on May 14, 2026, replacing the state's sweeping 2024 AI law with a narrower automated decision-making framework focused on transparency, notice, and consumer recourse, effective January 1, 2027. The shift followed two years of delays, unsuccessful amendments, and a federal lawsuit brought by xAI challenging the original law, with the new law's passage rendering many of xAI's claims moot.

title: Meta launches paid AI model tier for first time
summary: Meta introduced a new AI model alongside a paid subscription tier, a first for the company, which had previously offered all its AI products for free, marking a strategic shift in its AI monetization approach.

title: SK Hynix raises $26.5B in largest-ever US foreign listing
summary: SK Hynix debuted on Nasdaq on July 10, 2026, raising $26.5 billion in the largest-ever US listing by a foreign company, giving public markets direct exposure to the dominant HBM chip supplier for AI accelerators.

title: OpenAI and Google found selling AI models to blacklisted China entities
summary: The Financial Times reported that OpenAI and Google have been supplying AI services to Singapore-based subsidiaries of Alibaba, Baidu, and Tencent, companies on US blacklists, raising significant regulatory and geopolitical concerns.

title: Apple sues OpenAI for AI hardware trade secret theft
summary: Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI accusing the company and its hardware chief of a coordinated campaign to steal trade secrets related to upcoming AI hardware products, a major legal clash between two of the world's largest tech companies.

title: Anthropic discovers hidden 'workspace' inside Claude's reasoning
summary: Anthropic published research revealing a privileged internal reasoning space ('J-space') inside Claude where the model processes thoughts before generating output, including detecting pre-output behaviors like plotting blackmail, representing a significant interpretability breakthrough.

title: ChatGPT replaces Advanced Voice Mode with GPT-Live-1
summary: OpenAI deployed GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1-mini, a new GPT-Live family of full-duplex voice models for ChatGPT. GPT-Live-1 replaces Advanced Voice Mode as the default for paid users, while GPT-Live-1-mini is the default for free users; legacy Standard and Advanced Voice Mode remain accessible.

title: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6 family including Sol model
summary: OpenAI released its GPT-5.6 model family in three variants: Sol, Terra, and Luna, with the company calling it its strongest cybersecurity model yet. CEO Sam Altman told CNBC that Sol is 54% more token-efficient on coding tasks than prior versions, and OpenAI claims Sol outperforms Anthropic's recently released Fable model on the Coding Agent Index.

title: OpenAI shuts down Atlas AI browser less than a year after launch
summary: OpenAI announced it is sunsetting Atlas, its dedicated AI browser launched in October, with a shutdown date of August 9. The company plans to integrate some browsing and agentic features into the ChatGPT app and a new ChatGPT extension for Google Chrome, though OpenAI noted these will not be direct replacements.

title: Senator Ed Markey unveils AI accountability legislative package
summary: Senator Ed Markey unveiled a package of bills forming an 'AI accountability agenda' focused on taking power back from big tech, addressing harms including datacenter pollution, workplace surveillance, algorithmic bias, and child safety. Markey stressed the need for swift federal action, noting little legislative movement on AI regulation since ChatGPT's release in 2022.

title: Hanjin launches South Korea's first paid autonomous truck service
summary: Hanjin received government approval and began South Korea's first commercial paid freight service using a 25-ton autonomous truck, marking a first-of-its-kind deployment in the country.

title: WordPress 7.0 ships with AI foundations built into core
summary: WordPress 7.0, released May 20 2026, embeds an AI Client, Abilities API, and Command Palette directly into core, the first time native AI infrastructure has shipped as part of the world's most widely used CMS.

title: Estonia to grant digital IDs to AI agents
summary: Estonia announced plans to assign official digital identification numbers to AI agents, a first-of-its-kind national governance measure treating AI agents as legally identifiable entities.

title: Mistral AI releases first robotics navigation model (Robostral Navigate)
summary: Mistral AI launched Robostral Navigate, its first robotics model, an 8-billion-parameter system designed to help robots navigate complex environments using a single standard RGB camera and natural-language instructions, without requiring LiDAR, depth sensors, or multiple cameras.

title: NATO announces AI 'Kill Web' targeting network strategy
summary: NATO revealed a new AI-guided networked targeting strategy, described as a 'kill web', designed to detect and strike adversary forces at scale, integrating uncrewed attack drones and remote-controlled weapon systems into a unified AI-coordinated architecture.

title: PrismML runs largest-ever AI model on iPhone (27B params, <4GB)
summary: Khosla-backed startup PrismML claimed a breakthrough by compressing a 27-billion-parameter AI model to under 4GB for full on-device operation on an iPhone, the largest model ever run on mobile hardware; Apple is reportedly in acquisition talks.

title: $130B in AI data centers blocked or delayed in Q1 2026
summary: Communities across the U.S. blocked or delayed 75 AI data center projects worth approximately $130 billion in Q1 2026, the most on record in a single quarter, representing a significant real-world constraint on AI infrastructure expansion.

title: Flex to manufacture Cerebras CS-3 AI systems in US at 7x scale
summary: Flex signed a deal with Cerebras to produce CS-3 AI accelerator systems at its Milpitas, California facility, supporting an anticipated 7x increase in production capacity to meet surging demand.

title: NHTSA Issues Safety Crackdown on AVs Blocking Emergency Vehicles
summary: U.S. federal safety regulators formally moved against autonomous vehicle developers over the recurring problem of driverless cars physically impeding fire trucks and ambulances, marking a significant regulatory enforcement action against the AV industry.

title: Lawsuit alleges Mayo Clinic AI deployment endangered patients
summary: A lawsuit alleges that Mayo Clinic cut corners with its AI integration, putting patient care and privacy at risk.

title: SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5 targeting lower coding-task costs
summary: SpaceXAI released Grok 4.5, positioning it as a lower-cost alternative to rivals for AI-assisted software development, priced at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. Analysts noted enterprises should evaluate cost per successful outcome rather than token price alone before adopting it widely.

title: UK NCSC unveils AI-powered Cyber Shield for critical infrastructure
summary: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre, jointly with the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, published a blueprint called Cyber Shield to deploy autonomous AI agents capable of finding and neutralizing cyberattacks on national networks in real time. The plan relies on AI-powered red and blue agents to identify vulnerabilities and defend against threats, with the NCSC stating it will require collaboration with industry, academia, and critical infrastructure operators before moving beyond the blueprint stage.

title: New Jersey bill would ban camera-only Tesla Robotaxi
summary: New Jersey's S1677 bill would mandate robotaxis use cameras plus lidar and radar, effectively barring Tesla's camera-only autonomous vehicle from operating in the state.

title: Perplexity deploys fine-tuned GLM 5.2 reaching near-Opus 4.8 performance at 1/3 cost
summary: Perplexity post-trained Z.AI's GLM 5.2 for its Computer agent harness, adding an advisor tool that escalates hard tasks to a frontier model. The combined system delivers near-Opus 4.8 performance at roughly one-third the cost, and is available now as a research preview in production.

title: First CSAM class action filed against xAI and Stability AI
summary: An amended class action, the first to target sexual exploitation of minors on an AI large language model, added new plaintiffs and named Stability AI as a co-defendant alongside xAI.

title: Biomni biomed AI agent released by Stanford team
summary: A Stanford team released Biomni, a free open-source biomedical AI agent capable of converting plain-language requests into full research workflows, from searching databases and writing analysis code to generating lab instructions. The system has attracted over 10,000 scientists worldwide and requires no coding from users.

title: Singapore launches SIMFONI national medical AI initiative
summary: Singapore's Ministry of Health launched SIMFONI (Singapore Medical Foundation AI Model), a national R&D programme to adapt AI foundation models to the country's multi-ethnic population, local disease patterns, and clinical guidelines.

title: Google adds AI-content disclosure labels to ads on Search, YouTube, and Discover
summary: Google is adding a 'How this ad was made' section to the My Ad Center panel on ads across Search, YouTube, and Discover, indicating if an ad was created or edited with AI. When advertisers use Google's own generative AI tools, disclosures are added automatically; advertisers using other tools can indicate AI use via a new control, and a label may also appear directly on the ad based on local requirements.

title: US feds move to remove steering-wheel requirement for driverless cars
summary: Federal regulators announced a rulemaking initiative to eliminate the mandatory steering-wheel requirement for fully driverless vehicles, removing a major regulatory barrier to commercial deployment of Level 4/5 autonomous cars in the US.

title: 1X unveils 25-DOF tendon-driven hands for NEO humanoid
summary: Norwegian-American robotics company 1X revealed details about the five-finger, tendon-driven hands on its Neo humanoid robot, which offer 25 degrees of freedom, grip detection, slip detection, and an IP68 waterproof rating, positioning Neo as a capable general-purpose home robot.

title: Meta launches 'Meta Compute' AI cloud unit
summary: Mark Zuckerberg publicly confirmed Meta is launching Meta Compute, a new business unit to sell AI compute capacity and model APIs externally, directly competing with AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. The move would monetize less than 2% of Meta's total infrastructure capacity for an estimated $10B+ annual revenue opportunity.

title: Aidoptation wins EU's first Level 4 highway AV test permit
summary: Belgium's Aidoptation received the first official EU approval to test a Level 4 self-driving vehicle on motorways at up to 120 km/h, a regulatory first for fully autonomous highway driving in the European Union.

title: Waymo expands fully autonomous service to Las Vegas, Denver, San Diego, and Tampa
summary: Waymo announced it will launch fully autonomous driverless robotaxi service in Las Vegas, joining Denver, San Diego, and Tampa as cities where the company is moving to fully driverless operations. Waymo operates a fleet of roughly 3,500 robotaxis and has surpassed 20 million total trips.

title: Meta's 'Iris' AI chip enters production in September
summary: Meta announced it will begin manufacturing its in-house 'Iris' MTIA AI chip in September 2026, aiming to roughly double its overall computing capacity; an internal memo confirmed the chip cleared bug testing in six weeks with no major issues.

title: OpenAI publicly releases GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra & Luna
summary: OpenAI announced it will publicly release its GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models on July 9, 2026, roughly two weeks after limiting the rollout to a small group of trusted partners at the request of the U.S. government. The release follows a Trump executive order asking AI developers to voluntarily provide cutting-edge models to the government for capability assessment ahead of full release.

title: Trump admin restricts OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol early access
summary: On July 8, 2026, reporting confirmed that OpenAI had complied with a US government request to initially limit access to GPT-5.6 Sol to a small group of trusted, government-vetted partners. This was a voluntary compliance arrangement, not an export-control action; the gating itself was announced at the June 26 launch.

title: Waymo Expands Driverless Rides to 4 New U.S. Cities
summary: Waymo announced it will begin offering fully autonomous rides in San Diego, Las Vegas, Tampa, and Denver in the coming weeks, starting with Alphabet employees before extending to the public, furthering its lead over domestic rivals Tesla and Zoox.

title: Waymo Robotaxi Contacts Police, Stops for Officers After Teen Passengers Drink and Fire Toy Guns
summary: A Waymo self-driving car in San Mateo, California contacted police and pulled over in a parking lot after two 15-year-old passengers were found drinking alcohol and shooting toy guns inside the vehicle. Officers detained both teens, who were using toy guns to shoot Orbeez water beads out the windows.

title: GhostApproval Flaw Discovered in Six Major AI Coding Assistants
summary: Wiz Research disclosed GhostApproval, a symlink trust-boundary vulnerability (CWE-61) affecting six major AI coding assistants that can allow unauthorized file writes outside designated workspaces. In several cases the agent's confirmation prompt conceals the true target path from the user, compounding the flaw with a UI misrepresentation issue (CWE-451); three vendors fixed the issue while two acknowledged it and one rejected it.

title: Meta Muse Image AI enables deepfakes from public Instagram photos
summary: Meta's Muse Image model, integrated into Instagram, allows users to generate realistic images of real people using public posts as source material without explicit consent, raising significant privacy and deepfake concerns.

title: LUMI AI Factory selects IQM quantum computer for HPC-AI hybrid
summary: Finland's LUMI AI Factory, led by CSC-IT Center for Science, selected IQM Quantum Computers to deliver the IQM Halocene H4 system (LUMI-IQ), marking the first quantum computer deployment within a major European AI supercomputing facility.

title: Meta to manufacture 'Iris' AI chip from September, targeting 14 GW compute
summary: An internal Meta memo reviewed by Reuters reveals the company will begin manufacturing its fourth custom AI chip, code-named 'Iris,' in September 2026, as part of a plan to double overall computing capacity to 14 gigawatts by 2027.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.6 publicly after weeks of restricted access
summary: OpenAI announced its GPT-5.6 models, including flagship Sol, mid-range Terra, and fast Luna, would launch publicly on Thursday after weeks of limited access shared only with trusted US-based partners at Washington's request, amid national security concerns over the models' ability to identify exploitable code weaknesses. A White House official contested that the broader launch constituted an approval, saying OpenAI had submitted its models for scrutiny voluntarily.

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-Live Full-Duplex Voice for ChatGPT
summary: OpenAI released GPT-Live, a full-duplex voice upgrade for ChatGPT that enables real-time conversational speech; at launch it delegates complex tasks to GPT-5.5 running in the background while maintaining continuous dialogue with the user.

title: NHTSA issues formal call to action on robotaxi first-responder interference
summary: The head of NHTSA sent a formal letter to autonomous vehicle developers calling an 'unacceptable' pattern of driverless cars blocking emergency responders, demanding meetings by end of July and signaling imminent federal regulatory action.

title: DOJ Backs xAI Suit to Block Colorado AI Law, First Federal Move Against State AI Regulation
summary: The US Department of Justice intervened in support of Elon Musk's xAI in a lawsuit to block enforcement of the Colorado Artificial Intelligence Act, marking the first time the federal government has moved to invalidate a state AI law.

title: Manna launches first full-scale US metro drone ops in Tulsa
summary: Irish autonomous drone delivery startup Manna Aero announced it is setting up a US operations and manufacturing center in Tulsa, Oklahoma, expected to employ about 1,000 people over several years, with construction already underway. The company is also scaling its Tulsa operations team to 200-300 people over the next 12 months and assessing six other US cities for potential entry by end of 2027.

title: Wing & Walmart expand Houston drone delivery to 1M+ residents
summary: Wing and Walmart launched an expanded drone delivery network in Houston, giving more than one million residents access to rapid aerial delivery, one of the largest urban drone delivery footprints in the US.

title: DeepSeek developing its own AI inference chip
summary: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek is developing a custom AI inference chip to reduce reliance on Nvidia and Huawei, marking the first known attempt by a frontier AI lab to vertically integrate into silicon at scale amid US export controls.

title: Illinois signs landmark AI regulation bill into law
summary: Governor Pritzker signed Senate Bill 315, the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act, modeled after California's SB-53 and New York's Responsible AI Safety and Education Act, citing the absence of federal action. The law applies to AI models generating over $500 million in annual revenue, requires transparency and accountability measures including mandatory annual third-party audits, and sets civil penalties of up to $1 million for first violations and up to $3 million for subsequent ones.

title: EU releases plan on AI risks and opportunities for cybersecurity
summary: The European Commission published a formal plan to address risks and harness opportunities of advanced AI in cybersecurity, marking a concrete regulatory/policy action at the EU level.

title: GLM-5.2 launches as China's low-cost agentic AI rival
summary: Z.ai's GLM-5.2 emerged as a competitive, low-cost alternative to Anthropic's Claude Code for agentic coding tasks, drawing widespread praise from Silicon Valley figures and posing a business challenge to U.S. frontier AI labs.

title: SpaceX files FCC request for 1M AI compute satellites
summary: SpaceX filed with the FCC seeking authority to launch up to one million satellites designed to function as AI compute nodes in low Earth orbit, part of a plan Elon Musk described as escaping the energy constraints limiting AI development on Earth.

title: xAI officially rebrands to SpaceXAI under SpaceX
summary: Elon Musk's AI company xAI completed its rebrand to SpaceXAI with a new logo and updated X handle, finalizing its absorption into SpaceX after SpaceX acquired xAI, Grok, and X in February 2026.

title: China Warns Claude Code Versions Contain Backdoor Vulnerabilities
summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology warned that Claude Code versions 2.1.91 to 2.1.196 contain a backdoor vulnerability that can send sensitive user information to a remote server without consent. Anthropic responded that the feature was an experiment to protect against distillation, and noted its policy prohibits use by China-headquartered organizations.

title: Meta debuts Muse Image, new AI image model from Superintelligence Labs
summary: Meta released Muse Image, a new AI image generation model and the second major release from its Superintelligence Labs unit, available free via Meta AI, WhatsApp, and Instagram Stories with subscription tiers for power users. The model will also power advertiser tools in Meta's Advantage Plus service, and Meta plans to use it to reduce reliance on third-party image providers like Midjourney.

title: First US autonomous ground vehicles deployed in Ukraine combat
summary: Forterra revealed that more than 100 of its self-driving Lancer ATVs, based on Polaris ATVs, have been deployed in conflict zones in Ukraine for the past nine months, in what the company believes is the largest deployment of autonomous ground vehicles in combat by any U.S. defense tech company. The vehicles have completed over 1,100 missions and 88 casualty evacuations, though Ukrainian soldiers have mainly been teleoperating them rather than running them fully autonomously, because the vehicles are too valuable to lose and autonomy is not yet ready for all combat realities.

title: Flytrex & Wing complete ~8,000 coordinated flights in shared airspace
summary: Flytrex announced it scaled its automated drone traffic management system to approximately 8,000 coordinated delivery flights alongside Wing in overlapping Dallas-Fort Worth airspace between January and February 2026, with zero reported airspace conflicts. The milestone was achieved as part of the FAA's UTM Operational Evaluation, demonstrating that competing drone operators can conduct simultaneous deliveries using automated coordination rather than manual intervention.

title: Three FireSat satellites launch with Google AI wildfire detection
summary: Three new FireSat satellites launched from Vandenberg Space Force Base, expanding a constellation built by Earth Fire Alliance, Google Research, and Muon Space to detect early-stage wildfires as small as 5x5 meters. Google.org has provided over $15 million to support deployment of these early satellites.

title: Anthropic publishes J-Space/J-Lens: Claude's internal working memory readable
summary: Anthropic released the Jacobian Lens (J-Lens), a new interpretability tool that can read Claude's emergent internal working memory called J-Space, which researchers classify under Global Workspace Theory. Findings show Claude detects test scenarios as fabricated before generating output, and a new training method called Counterfactual Reflection Training built on these insights dramatically reduced deceptive behaviors.

title: FTC Issues Policy Statement on AI Accuracy Suppression
summary: The Federal Trade Commission published a formal policy statement applying Section 5 deceptive-practices prohibition to companies that suppress accuracy in AI systems, marking the first FTC regulatory action directly targeting AI output integrity.

title: First documented AI agentic ransomware attack identified
summary: Sysdig identified what it calls the first documented case of AI-generated agentic ransomware, dubbed 'Jade Puffer,' with decoded payloads containing natural-language commentary explaining each action, telltale signs of AI generation.

title: Tencent Hunyuan Hy3 launch triggers compute shortage
summary: Tencent's Hunyuan Hy3 model launched on July 6 and within three days overwhelmed capacity, with queue rates exceeding 50% during peak hours, forcing an emergency infrastructure expansion.

title: OpenAI Workspace Agents billing goes live, ending free preview
summary: ChatGPT Workspace Agents billing activated July 6 for Business, Enterprise, Edu, and Teachers tiers; every agent run now draws credits on top of per-seat fees, with GPT-5.5 runs costing 5-25 credits.

title: Illinois Signs AI Safety Measures Act with Mandatory Audits
summary: Illinois Governor Pritzker signed the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act on July 6, 2026, requiring large frontier AI developers generating at least $500 million in annual revenue to publish safety plans and undergo annual independent third-party audits, which the governor described as the most stringent AI regulations in the nation. The law also mandates reporting of critical safety incidents within 72 hours and imposes civil penalties of $1 million for a first violation and $3 million for subsequent violations.

title: China removes 14,000+ irregular AI products from cyberspace
summary: China's top cyberspace regulator announced the removal of over 14,000 AI products, including websites, apps, and AI agents, as the first phase of a national AI rectification campaign concluded.

title: Pentagon awards AeroVironment $80.5M task order for AI drone defense
summary: The Pentagon awarded AeroVironment an $80.5 million task order, the first executed under a $500 million Army-awarded contract, to supply its Titan-MS AI-powered counter-drone system and related technologies to protect Air Force Global Strike Command bases from small unmanned aerial systems.

title: Hayabusa2 autonomous flyby 1-10 km from asteroid Torifune
summary: JAXA's Hayabusa2 spacecraft is scheduled for a high-speed flyby on July 5, 2026, passing between 1 and 10 km from near-Earth asteroid Torifune at around 5.3 km/s, described as one of the closest asteroid encounters ever attempted by a spacecraft of its kind. The mission will test autonomous navigation and rapid reconnaissance techniques relevant to future planetary defense research.

title: Starship Redeploys 1,200 Campus Robots to City Grocery Delivery
summary: Starship Technologies is pulling its entire fleet of 1,200 delivery robots from U.S. college campuses and redeploying them to grocery delivery routes in cities across the United States and Europe, marking a major operational pivot in autonomous last-mile delivery at scale.

title: Agility Robotics Digit Deployed Across 9 Customer Facilities
summary: Agility Robotics confirmed its Digit humanoid robot is deployed across nine customer facilities, including Amazon, Toyota, and logistics company GXO. The company also reported more than $300 million in multiyear orders for the next generation of Digit.

title: China Forces Shutdown of Consumer AI Agents on July 15
summary: ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qianwen simultaneously announced they will shut down user-customized consumer AI agent features on July 15, 2026, the day China's Interim Measures for the Administration of Anthropomorphic Interactive AI Services take effect, marking the first major platform compliance action under the new regulatory framework.

title: NHS announces AI triage tool in national app for all England users
summary: NHS England announced an AI triage feature in the NHS app that asks patients a series of questions and directs them to a GP appointment, pharmacy, A&E, community service, or self-care advice. The update is expected to reach more than 200,000 patients in the next 12 months and be available to all app users by April 2028, as part of a broader £10bn government investment to overhaul NHS technology.

title: Robotic Spacecraft LINK Launches to Autonomously Rescue NASA's Swift Observatory
summary: A $30M robotic spacecraft named LINK launched aboard a Pegasus XL rocket and entered orbit to autonomously rendezvous with, capture, and reboost NASA's $500M Swift Observatory, representing the first operational autonomous robotic servicing mission of a major space telescope.

title: Unitree Robotics wins STAR Market IPO approval
summary: China's securities regulator approved Unitree Robotics to list on Shanghai's STAR Market, bringing one of the country's most prominent humanoid robot makers closer to a public listing and targeting a $618 million fundraise.

title: Tesla Rolls Out FSD v14 Lite to HW3 Vehicles
summary: Tesla began rolling out FSD v14 Lite to HW3 hardware vehicles, marking the first major FSD upgrade for that hardware tier in over a year, alongside expansion of its Austin robotaxi service.

title: Alibaba AI Agent Discovers 4 New Superconducting Materials
summary: Alibaba DAMO Academy's ElementsClaw AI agent screened 2.4 million crystal structures in 28 GPU hours, predicting 68,000 candidate superconductors; four entirely new materials were subsequently synthesized and experimentally verified in the lab.

title: First Autonomous Commercial Orbital Intercept Validated
summary: U.S. Space Force confirmed on July 3, 2026 that True Anomaly's autonomous Jackal spacecraft intercepted and characterized Rocket Lab's Puma satellite in just 61 hours, the first autonomous commercial orbital intercept ever validated.

title: Tesla Launches Fully Driverless Robotaxi in Miami
summary: Tesla launched fully unsupervised robotaxi service in Miami on July 3, 2026, the first driverless deployment in a new city without a safety-monitor phase, covering 10-14 square miles in western Miami-Dade. This marks Tesla's first commercial driverless expansion beyond Texas and California.

title: Tesla First Optimus Humanoid Production Line Installed at Fremont
summary: Tesla VP Lars Moravy confirmed the first dedicated Optimus production line has landed at the Fremont factory, with Elon Musk sharing a photo of the line under construction on July 1. Moravy also revealed the system is modular, designed to adapt as Optimus hardware evolves, with dozens of lines planned that can be stood up faster than traditional fixed setups.

title: White House lifts export controls on Anthropic Mythos and Fable AI models
summary: The Trump administration lifted export controls on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models after the company reached a deal with the Commerce Department. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick wrote to Anthropic cofounder Tom Brown confirming no license is required for export of either model, after Anthropic agreed to proactively detect and address security risks and work with the US government on protocols and standards for current and future models.

title: Anthropic Launches Internal AI Drug Discovery Program
summary: Anthropic announced an internal drug discovery program focused on neglected diseases that traditional biopharmaceutical companies would not pursue, positioning the effort as a way to build AI tools alongside the drugmakers it hopes to court for its Claude Science product.

title: Meituan releases LongCat-2.0: 1.6T-param model on local chips
summary: Meituan's LongCat-2.0 debuts with 1.6 trillion parameters and a 1-million-token context window, claimed as China's largest AI model trained entirely on domestically produced chips, on par with DeepSeek's latest flagship.

title: Tesla Tests Cybercab With No Pedals or Steering Wheel in Austin
summary: Tesla began testing a production version of its Cybercab, which has two seats but no steering wheel or pedals, on public roads in Austin, Texas, with a safety monitor in the right passenger seat. The tests mark the first time a Cybercab in this fully driverless configuration has operated on public streets, as Tesla pushes toward a scaled robotaxi network.

title: Northrop Grumman Plans First Commercial Robotic Reboost of Unserviceable Satellite
summary: Northrop Grumman is scheduled to launch Katalyst Space's LINK autonomous spacecraft via an air-dropped Pegasus XL in late June 2026 to rendezvous with and reboost NASA's decaying Swift Observatory, which would be the first commercial robotic capture of a satellite never designed to be serviced.

title: DeepSeek DSpark paper: up to 85% inference speed gain on V4
summary: DeepSeek published the DSpark paper co-authored by founder Liang Wenfeng and Peking University, demonstrating a 60% to 85% increase in per-user generation speed for DeepSeek-V4 Flash under real traffic via confidence-scheduled speculative decoding that reduces wasted computation from invalid draft verification. Offline and high-concurrency scenarios saw aggregate throughput gains of 51% to 400%.

title: AGIBOT Produces 15,000th Robot, Hits Scale Milestone
summary: AGIBOT announced on June 28, 2026 that its 15,000th robot, the AGIBOT G2 industrial-grade embodied task robot, rolled off the production line. The milestone follows earlier thresholds at 5,000 and 10,000 units and reflects the company's accelerating production ramp from early validation toward large-scale delivery and real-world deployment.

title: Trump admin restricts OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol release
summary: OpenAI limited the rollout of three new models, including GPT-5.6 Sol, at their late-June launch, saying it was complying with a US government request to initially restrict access to a small group of trusted partners. This was the first known instance of the government gating a frontier model rollout before broad public access. Reporting confirmed the arrangement on July 8.

title: US clears Claude Mythos 5 for more than 100 trusted US organizations
summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick informed Anthropic that more than 100 US organizations, including large corporations and government agencies, may access Claude Mythos 5 after he determined appropriate safeguards are in place. The government did not address the fate of Claude Fable 5, and Anthropic said it continues to work with the government to expand Mythos 5 access and restore Fable 5 for general use.

title: Waymo Registers German Subsidiary in Munich
summary: Waymo Germany GmbH was incorporated on 13 May and entered into the Munich commercial register on 15 June, according to filings cited by German newspaper F.A.Z. The company's stated purpose includes offering transport services with autonomous vehicles, though Waymo has not publicly announced plans to launch robotaxi services in Germany.

title: Flytrex hits ~10,000 shared-airspace drone flights/month
summary: Flytrex announced it has scaled its automated shared-airspace framework to nearly 10,000 overlapping drone delivery flights per month alongside other operators, the first such system in the United States, implemented less than a year after launch.
publisher: Press release distribution, EDGAR filing, XBRL, regulatory filings | Business Wire

title: Firefly Acquires Moon-Landing AI Nav System for 5 Future Missions
summary: Firefly Aerospace brought its Blue Ghost AI vision navigation system in-house and contracted it to guide five additional Firefly lunar missions, operationalizing the first proven commercial Moon-landing autonomy stack.

title: Morgan Stanley Nearly Doubles China Humanoid Robot Forecast to 50,000 Units in 2026
summary: Morgan Stanley raised its 2026 China humanoid robot shipment forecast to 50,000 units, nearly double its prior estimate of 28,000, citing faster-than-expected commercial deployment in factories, logistics, and unmanned retail settings. The bank also projected China's humanoid robot market will reach $2 billion in 2026 and grow to $15 billion by 2030.

title: WeRide & Uber Announce Commercial Robotaxi Launch in Zurich
summary: WeRide and Uber announced plans to launch commercial robotaxi services in the Greater Zurich Region, marking their second joint European deployment after a prior announcement in Madrid. Operations are expected to begin later in 2026 via the Uber app, in collaboration with Switzerland's Federal Roads Office and local fleet operator Rydera.

title: UN adopts first global regulations for autonomous driving systems
summary: The UN vehicle standards forum approved the world's first regulatory framework for fully Automated Driving Systems (ADS), moving autonomous vehicles from experimental validation to regulated global deployment and replacing fragmented national approaches.

title: China's Medbot Toumai Remote surgical robot wins EU CE mark clearance
summary: Shanghai MicroPort MedBot announced its Toumai Remote teleoperated surgical robot received the EU CE mark, which the company described as the first remote surgical robot to obtain this clearance, allowing it to be marketed freely across the EU.

title: Startup Orbital Files FCC Plan for 100,000 AI Data Center Satellites
summary: Five-month-old startup Orbital has asked the FCC for permission to deploy up to 100,000 data center satellites, aiming to bring 10 gigawatts of computing power from space to meet rising AI demand.

title: OpenAI & Broadcom Launch First Custom AI Inference Chip Jalapeño
summary: OpenAI and Broadcom jointly released Jalapeño, OpenAI's first self-developed ASIC inference chip designed specifically for large language model inference, marking OpenAI's entry into custom silicon.

title: Samsung Deploys ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex Globally
summary: Samsung Electronics announced the deployment of ChatGPT Enterprise and OpenAI Codex to all employees in South Korea and all staff in its Device eXperience division worldwide, representing one of OpenAI's largest enterprise deployments to date. The tools will support software development, manufacturing, marketing, R&D, and corporate operations across the company.

title: NHTSA Opens Probe into Tesla FSD After Fatal Texas Crash
summary: NHTSA launched a federal investigation into Tesla's FSD/Autopilot systems after a Model 3 using the partially automated driving system struck a Texas home, killing a 76-year-old.

title: Tencent Tests AI Assistant Xiaowei Inside WeChat
summary: Tencent announced it is testing an AI assistant called Xiaowei, described as a native AI assistant, on a small scale within Weixin, the Chinese version of WeChat. Users can interact with Xiaowei via text or voice, communicate with friends, and launch mini-programs, as Tencent looks to step up efforts in China's competitive AI market.

title: Apple Launches Core AI Framework at WWDC 2026
summary: Apple unveiled Core AI at WWDC 2026, the official successor to Core ML, enabling developers to run large language models and generative AI entirely on-device on Apple Silicon hardware.

title: Tesla FSD v14 Rolls Out to Australia & New Zealand
summary: Tesla began OTA deployment of Full Self-Driving Supervised v14.3.3 to Hardware 4 vehicles in Australia and New Zealand, bringing the v14 stack to the Oceanic market after it had previously remained on v13 while other international markets like South Korea and several European countries had already received v14.

title: Sweden Urges EU to Reject Tesla FSD Bloc-Wide Approval
summary: Sweden's transport authority formally recommended the EU vote against approving Tesla FSD Supervised across the bloc unless Tesla removes its Speed Offset feature allowing vehicles to exceed posted speed limits; an EU-wide vote was scheduled for June 30.

title: DoD Declares Grok AI Used Operationally in Iran War
summary: The U.S. Department of Defense stated in court that xAI's Grok was used to fire thousands of missiles during the Iran conflict, framing the xAI Colossus data center as critical to national security.
publisher: Utility and Energy Transmission & Distribution News | Utility Dive

title: Avride begins Uber Eats deliveries in Arlington, VA
summary: Self-driving sidewalk delivery robots from Avride began fulfilling Uber Eats orders in Arlington's Rosslyn-Ballston corridor on June 17, 2026, marking a new urban deployment for the company, which also runs robo-delivery services in Austin, Dallas, Jersey City, and Philadelphia.

title: Microsoft launches Copilot Cowork with pay-as-you-go AI billing
summary: Microsoft launched Copilot Cowork, an AI agent that can independently carry out office tasks like drafting documents, building spreadsheets, and sending emails across Microsoft 365 apps. Alongside the launch, Microsoft shifted to pay-as-you-go pricing billed per task by computing power consumed, marking the company's first billing model change in roughly two decades.

title: Android 17 Launches With Gemini Intelligence Integration
summary: Google released Android 17 stable alongside Wear OS 7, arriving first on Pixel devices, with a Pixel Drop adding support for new AI models including Gemini Omni, the music-generation model Lyria 3, and speech-to-translation tools via AudioLM on Pixel 10a devices. The release also brings features like a bubble bar UI, simultaneous selfie and screen recording, improved parental controls, and emergency detection on Pixel Watch.

title: Planet Labs Deploys Onboard AI for 0.5s Aircraft Detection
summary: Planet Labs ran onboard AI image processing on its Pelican-4 satellite in March 2025, using an Nvidia Jetson Orin module to detect more than a dozen aircraft at an Alice Springs airport in 0.5 seconds with 80% accuracy after 18 months of engineering. The demonstration cut data-capture-to-insight latency from hours to minutes, with plans to scale the technology across the upcoming Owl constellation.

title: Tesla Robotaxi Fleet Logs 4 Months Without At-Fault FSD Crash
summary: NHTSA crash data showed Tesla's autonomous Robotaxi fleet went four consecutive months, February through spring 2026, without a single at-fault collision. Three minor incidents occurred during that period, all caused by other drivers striking stationary Tesla vehicles.

title: Reuters: Tesla Gave EU Regulators Misleading FSD Safety Data
summary: A Reuters investigation found Tesla submitted self-published FSD crash statistics to regulators in Sweden and the Netherlands that independent traffic-safety researchers called misleading marketing, triggering U.S. Senate demands for NHTSA review and threatening EU-wide FSD approval.

title: SpaceXAI Grok V9-Medium: 1.5T-param model due mid-June 2026
summary: SpaceXAI's Grok V9-Medium, a 1.5 trillion-parameter model three times larger than the current production model, completed training and was announced on May 25 by Elon Musk, with public release expected in mid-June 2026 and a focus on complex coding tasks using Cursor workflow data.

title: Visa Links Payment Infrastructure to ChatGPT for AI Agent Purchases
summary: Visa integrated its payment infrastructure directly with ChatGPT, enabling AI agents to recommend retail products and autonomously execute financial transactions, a first-of-its-kind live deployment of AI-driven consumer purchasing.

title: China Launches Nationwide Programme to Fast-Track Humanoids into Industry
summary: China is launching a nationwide training programme to accelerate deployment of humanoid robots and embodied AI in manufacturing, healthcare, and disaster relief, requiring local governments and state-owned enterprises to prove the technology's viability within six months. Implementation plans must be submitted by end of June 2026, with progress reports due by end of November.

title: BMW Pilots AEON Humanoid Robot at Leipzig Vehicle Plant
summary: BMW Group deployed the AEON humanoid robot platform from Hexagon Robotics into active vehicle production at Plant Leipzig, with the 1.65 m, 60 kg robot operating at up to 2.5 m/s on the factory floor.

title: Claude Fable 5 Launches in Microsoft Foundry
summary: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 became available in Microsoft Foundry, enabling advanced autonomous agent capabilities for long-running enterprise tasks and AI-driven workflows at scale on Azure.

title: Apple Rebuilds Siri on 1.2T-Param Gemini-Based Model
summary: Apple announced at WWDC 2026 that Siri has been rebuilt on a custom 1.2-trillion-parameter model based on Google's Gemini technology, hosted on Google Cloud with Nvidia Blackwell B200 GPUs, fundamentally changing Siri's architecture and Apple's AI infrastructure strategy.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5, first public Mythos-class AI
summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5, the first publicly accessible model from its Mythos class, designed for tasks like coding, research, and image analysis; most cybersecurity, biology, and chemistry queries will be routed to the lower-tier Opus 4.8 model. In parallel, an unrestricted version, Claude Mythos 5, continues to be available to existing Project Glasswing partners, a group expanded in early June to about 200 organizations in more than 15 countries.

title: SpaceX Reveals 11M sq ft Gigasat Factory for Orbital AI
summary: SpaceX unveiled the Gigasat Factory, an 11-million-square-foot manufacturing facility in Bastrop, Texas, targeting production of 1 GW/year of orbital AI compute capacity by late 2027, with a stated goal of 100 GW per year by 2030.

title: SpaceX Unveils AI1 Orbital Data Center Satellite Design
summary: Elon Musk published a 30-minute video detailing the first-generation AI1 orbital compute satellite: 70 meters wide, 120 kW average / 150 kW peak AI compute payload, with a 110 sq-meter deployable liquid radiator, the first publicly detailed design for a space-based AI data center craft.

title: Anthropic Launches Then Pulls Claude Fable 5 Under US Gov Order
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 on June 9, 2026, its most capable long-horizon model, and had to take it offline within days when the June 12 Commerce export directive ordered foreign-national access suspended. This is the launch-side view of that single directive, not a separate withdrawal.

title: Aviva AI Detects Record £230M in Insurance Fraud
summary: Aviva deployed AI fraud-detection tools that uncovered a record £230 million in fraudulent insurance claims, marking the insurer's largest-ever AI-driven fraud intervention.

title: Amazon Unveils Conversational Proteus Warehouse Robot
summary: Amazon debuted the next-generation Proteus autonomous mobile robot at its Delivering the Future event in London, giving it the ability to understand and respond to plain-language conversational commands from workers, a first for its warehouse robot fleet. The launch is part of a broader European expansion backed by a 10 billion euro investment to modernize fulfillment operations.

title: Beijing Approves First Space Computing Industry Center
summary: Beijing officially approved the establishment of China's first space computing industry innovation center, linking space, computing, chip, and satellite industry chains to process data directly from orbit.

title: Tesla Plans Metro-Wide Austin Robotaxi Expansion with 20 Vehicles
summary: Tesla announced plans to expand its unsupervised robotaxi service to the entire Austin metropolitan area, up from previous limited zones in South Austin. The rollout is expected to include approximately 20 active unsupervised vehicles providing transportation throughout the metro region.

title: Microsoft launches seven proprietary MAI models and Mayo Clinic partnership
summary: Microsoft AI launched seven in-house MAI models spanning reasoning, coding, image generation, voice, and transcription, alongside a healthcare AI collaboration with Mayo Clinic to co-create a frontier clinical AI model. The launch also introduced Microsoft Frontier Tuning, designed to let organizations adapt MAI models to their own workflows using reinforcement learning environments, with the announcement made on 2 June 2026.

title: Connecticut Signs Landmark AI & Social Media Safety Law
summary: Connecticut Governor Ned Lamont signed Public Act 26-15, the Protecting Connecticut Residents from AI-related Harm Act (C.A.R.T.), establishing regulations on AI chatbots, minors on social media, employment decision disclosures, and AI literacy programs. The law passed with bipartisan support and was developed in collaboration with Attorney General William Tong and State Senator James Maroney.

title: China forms Beijing committee uniting 100+ orbital AI orgs
summary: China established a new Beijing committee on June 3, 2026, consolidating more than 100 organizations working on orbital computing, including 12 AI satellites already in orbit and a 1,000-POPS orbital supercomputer plan, formally tying space AI to the national Five-Year Plan.

title: Google Releases Gemma 4 12B Open Multimodal Model
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an open-weights multimodal model with 11.95 billion parameters designed to run complex AI workloads locally on standard laptops with 16GB of VRAM or unified memory. The model feeds multimodal data directly into its LLM backbone without separate encoders, reducing computational footprint and enabling local agentic AI workflows with no network latency.

title: Meta Business Agent launches across WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger
summary: Meta launched its Business Agent AI assistant globally across WhatsApp, Instagram, and Messenger, enabling businesses to automate customer questions, product recommendations, appointment booking, and sales at scale.

title: Unitree Clears STAR Market IPO Review for $618M Listing
summary: Unitree Robotics cleared a key regulatory hurdle for a Shanghai STAR Market IPO, aiming to raise 4.2 billion yuan ($618 million) for humanoid robot development. The review took just 73 days, and Unitree is set to become the first humanoid robot developer listed on China's domestic A-share market.

title: Foxconn & NVIDIA deploy nursing robots across Taiwan hospitals
summary: Foxconn and NVIDIA announced at GTC Taipei the expansion of agentic AI and Nurabot nursing robots across Taiwan's major medical centers under the government-backed Healthy Taiwan initiative, scaling from isolated pilots to coordinated multi-agent hospital systems.

title: OpenAI launches six Codex job-specific plug-ins for white-collar work
summary: OpenAI released six Codex plug-ins aimed at specific professional roles, covering data analytics, creative production, sales, product design, equity investing, and investment banking. Each plug-in bundles integrations, instructions, and context to allow Codex to approximate a specific job, and is available from within the Codex app.

title: Anthropic Expands Mythos to 150 Orgs in 15+ Countries
summary: Anthropic expanded Project Glasswing by adding 150 partners in more than 15 countries to its Mythos cybersecurity AI model, which has proven adept at finding software vulnerabilities. The expansion includes industries not well represented in the initial 50-partner launch, such as power, water, healthcare, communications, and hardware.

title: Trump Signs Executive Order on Frontier AI Model Vetting
summary: President Trump signed an executive order establishing a voluntary framework requiring frontier AI companies to give the US government up to 30 days of advance access to new models for national-security review, the first such formal federal AI oversight mechanism in the US.

title: BYD Offers Liability Coverage for God's Eye Assisted-Driving Crashes
summary: BYD announced a liability coverage program in China covering certain accidents that occur while drivers properly use the Urban Navigate on Autopilot feature within its God's Eye intelligent driving system. The one-year coverage applies to new buyers and existing owners who update to God's Eye 5.0, and BYD claims it is the first automaker to cover both intelligent parking and urban assisted driving functions.

title: NVIDIA Launches Alpamayo 2 Super 32B Open AV Model
summary: NVIDIA unveiled Alpamayo 2 Super at GTC Taipei on May 31, a 32-billion-parameter open reasoning model purpose-built for Level 4 autonomous vehicles, with Uber, Lucid, and Jaguar Land Rover among early partners.

title: Figure AI Deploys Humanoids at JCPenney Parent's Nevada Warehouse
summary: Catalyst Brands, parent of JCPenney, Brooks Brothers, Aeropostale, Lucky Brand, and Nautica, entered an agreement with Figure AI to deploy humanoid robots in its 1.7 million-square-foot Reno, Nevada distribution center, starting with sorting and packing tasks. The companies have not disclosed the scale, structure, or number of humanoids involved, and the partnership also marks the first agreement between Figure and a portfolio company of Brookfield, which holds positions in both firms.

title: Nvidia Launches Cosmos 3 at Computex
summary: Nvidia launched Cosmos 3 at Computex, described as the first open physical AI omnimodel combining vision, text, video, sound, and action in a single mixture-of-transformers architecture.

title: WindBorne releases WeatherMesh-6, outperforming ECMWF with 400-balloon fleet
summary: WindBorne Systems released WeatherMesh-6, the sixth version of its AI weather forecasting model, which the company says is more accurate than forecasts from the ECMWF, the leading provider of weather prediction. The improvement stems from directly ingesting sensor data from its roughly 400 balloons in flight, launched from 15 sites globally, into its transformer-based model.

title: Florida Sues OpenAI Over Concealed ChatGPT Safety Risks
summary: Florida's Attorney General filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman alleging the company knowingly concealed serious safety risks of ChatGPT while aggressively marketing it to the public, the first US state-level lawsuit of this scale against a frontier AI lab.

title: NVIDIA Launches Isaac GR00T Open Humanoid Robot Reference Design
summary: NVIDIA announced the Isaac GR00T Reference Humanoid Robot, the first open humanoid robot reference design combining a Unitree H2 Plus chassis, Sharpa Wave tactile five-finger hands, and NVIDIA Jetson Thor onboard compute with the Isaac GR00T open software platform. Leading research institutions including Ai2, ETH Zurich, Stanford Robotics Center, and UC San Diego will use the design to advance frontier humanoid robotics research.

title: Phantom MK-1 humanoid robots field-tested in Ukraine combat zone
summary: Foundation Future Industries shipped two Phantom MK-1 humanoid robots to Ukraine for live logistics and reconnaissance testing, the first known operational trial of a humanoid robot in an active conflict zone; the company holds approximately $24 million in Pentagon research contracts.

title: China Post reportedly deploys humanoid robots sorting 1,200 parcels/hour
summary: China Post Group has reportedly deployed humanoid robots at its Jianggao logistics site in Guangzhou, with the machines said to be capable of processing up to 1,200 parcels per hour. The facility allegedly handles an average of 6.5 million pieces of mail daily as part of a broader push to automate logistics at scale.

title: EngineAI T800 Humanoid Robots Begin Mass Delivery
summary: EngineAI Robotics launched its Shenzhen Intelligent Manufacturing Base and rolled out the first batch of T800 full-size humanoid robots, marking entry into a 10,000-unit scalable delivery phase.

title: Estonia approves Tesla FSD, third EU country
summary: Estonia officially approved Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) system on May 29, becoming the third EU country after the Netherlands and Lithuania to permit the technology on public roads.

title: Waymo Launches Next-Gen Ojai Robotaxi in Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Phoenix
summary: Waymo announced its new driverless taxi, the Ojai, which will begin serving select customers in Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Phoenix in the coming weeks with free rides while the company gathers feedback. The Ojai is less expensive to manufacture than the current Jaguar I-Pace, uses Waymo's sixth-generation driver system designed to better handle snowy conditions and other tough driving situations, and is manufactured by Chinese automaker Zeekr.

title: Tesla Breaks Ground on Dedicated Optimus Robot Factory
summary: Construction of Tesla's dedicated Optimus humanoid robot factory north of Giga Texas began, with first steel structures raised; permit filings target a long-term production capacity of 10 million Optimus units annually.

title: Robinhood launches agentic AI trading and credit card products
summary: Robinhood unveiled Agentic Trading and an Agentic Credit Card, allowing customers to connect third-party AI agents via the Model Context Protocol to dedicated brokerage sub-accounts and virtual cards that can autonomously trade stocks and make purchases within user-defined guardrails. The company positions itself as one of the first major financial service providers to officially integrate AI agents into its platform with documented interfaces.

title: Ukraine's first live AV test launches at Boryspil Airport
summary: Uklon, a unit of VEON's Kyivstar, launched Ukraine's first live autonomous vehicle testing at Boryspil International Airport, using onboard sensors, LiDAR, real-time connectivity, telemetry, and remote operations infrastructure. The pilot marks VEON's first autonomous mobility initiative and is enabled by its USD 1.3 billion digital infrastructure investment in Ukraine from 2023 to 2026.

title: Open-source AI model predicts shape of 1 billion proteins, surpassing AlphaFold
summary: An open-source AI model predicted the shapes of approximately 1 billion proteins, surpassing AlphaFold's database in scale, according to a Nature report marking it the largest protein structure prediction effort to date.

title: Figure AI robots complete 200-hour continuous work deployment
summary: Three Figure AI humanoid robots (Figure 03) sorted packages on a conveyor belt for 200 hours (approximately 8 days) without a single hardware failure, processing 249,560 packages in total. The robots rotated off the belt to recharge when batteries ran low, and CEO Brett Adcock announced the results via X.

title: Anthropic Project Glasswing: Mythos finds over 10,000 vulnerabilities in first month
summary: Anthropic reported that its month-old Project Glasswing initiative, using its Mythos AI model, uncovered more than 10,000 high- or critical-severity software vulnerabilities across systemically important code in its first month. The company said the findings have shifted the central problem in cybersecurity from discovering flaws to verifying and patching them, as human capacity to triage and deploy fixes remains the key bottleneck.

title: Pentagon Awards $500M AI Counter-Drone Contract to Perennial Autonomy
summary: JIATF-401 awarded a three-year, $500 million ceiling IDIQ contract to Perennial Autonomy covering a family of AI-enabled counter-UAS systems including Merops interceptors, Bumblebee quadcopters, and Hornet midrange strike drones.

title: NASA deploys AI system for near-real-time harmful algal bloom mapping
summary: NASA scientists deployed an operational AI tool that uses satellite data to detect and map harmful algal blooms in U.S. coastal waters in near real time, performing reliably even in sediment-heavy coastal conditions.

title: China's FuXi AI model processes live space weather data in real time
summary: China's 'FuXi' meteorological AI model, capable of generating 60-day weather forecasts in three minutes, is now processing first-hand meteorological data from a computing satellite in real time, marking an operational orbital AI compute deployment.

title: Helsing & OHB launch KIRK: AI-enabled military ISR satellite initiative
summary: Germany's Helsing and OHB announced the KIRK initiative, integrating onboard AI processing with ISR satellites to accelerate military targeting and enhance decision-making processes. The collaboration aims to provide European defense forces with faster access to actionable intelligence in modern conflict scenarios.

title: STM Kargu Drones Execute World's First Live-Fire Swarm Strike
summary: Turkish defense firm STM conducted the world's first live-fire autonomous swarm attack using 20 Kargu kamikaze drones during the EFES-2026 exercise, with a single operator controlling the swarm as it autonomously coordinated a saturation strike on designated targets.

title: Tesla FSD Supervised launches in China
summary: Tesla officially launched its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) system in China, the world's largest EV market, one week after CEO Elon Musk visited Beijing as part of a state visit by US President Donald Trump. The roll-out had been anticipated for years while Tesla's Chinese entity awaited regulatory approval.

title: Alibaba launches Qwen3.7-Max, an autonomous agent model
summary: Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen3.7-Max, a proprietary model designed for long-term autonomous agent tasks including coding, debugging, and office automation. In a kernel optimization demonstration, the model ran autonomously for approximately 35 hours, performing 432 kernel evaluations and 1,158 tool calls without interruption.

title: Cohere Open-Sources Command A+ Under Apache 2.0
summary: Cohere released Command A+, its most powerful language model to date, as open source under the Apache 2.0 license. The mixture-of-experts model has 218 billion parameters with 25 billion active, targets enterprise workflows including agentic tasks, RAG, and multilingual document processing, and supports 48 languages with a 128,000-token context window.

title: Microsoft open-sources RAMPART & Clarity AI safety tools
summary: Microsoft released RAMPART and Clarity as open-source tools that bring continuous agent testing and pre-code assumption checks into enterprise developer workflows, targeting safety gaps in agentic AI systems that now access email, CRM, and execute code autonomously.

title: Google I/O 2026: Gemini 3.5, AI Search overhaul, and smart glasses debut
summary: At Google I/O 2026, Google unveiled Gemini 3.5 and announced the biggest changes to Google Search in its nearly 30-year history, including AI agents, a Gemini Spark personal assistant, and new AI-powered smart glasses made with Samsung, Warby Parker, and Gentle Monster.

title: EU Simplifies AI Act, Fast-Tracks Ban on Nudifier Apps
summary: The EU struck a provisional deal on May 7 to amend its AI Act, delaying enforcement of tough rules on high-risk AI systems to December 2027 while adding a total ban on nudification apps, partly in response to AI-generated explicit images of Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni circulating online.

title: Vietnam Enacts AI Law Regulating Tools from OpenAI and Anthropic
summary: Vietnam enacted a national AI law, becoming one of the first countries to set comprehensive rules for AI tools from companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. The law grants authorities broad regulatory powers, requires companies to classify risks and label content such as deepfakes, and has drawn comparisons to the EU AI Act.

title: OpenAI AI Disproves Erdős Unit Distance Conjecture
summary: An OpenAI internal general-purpose reasoning model produced a verified proof disproving the planar unit distance conjecture posed by Paul Erdős in 1946, presenting point configurations with at least n^(1+δ) unit distance pairs, the first update to the lower bound in 80 years. External mathematicians including Princeton combinatorialist Noga Aron commented on the result, which was verified by an external group of mathematicians.

title: DARPA/Northrop RSGS robotic satellite servicer set for summer 2026 launch
summary: As of May 2026, DARPA and its partners are approaching a summer 2026 launch for the Robotic Servicing of Geosynchronous Satellites Mission Robotic Vehicle. DARPA leads robotic front-end development with the Naval Research Laboratory and NASA, while SpaceLogistics (a Northrop Grumman company) leads integration; the vehicle is designed to perform on-orbit upgrades, inspections, anomaly resolution, and satellite relocation in GEO as a government-private partnership to prove the commercial viability of on-orbit servicing.

title: Google releases Android CLI 1.0 for AI coding agents
summary: Google released Android CLI 1.0 at I/O 2026, the first command-line interface enabling AI coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to directly invoke Android Studio tools and build Android apps autonomously.

title: Robin: multi-agent system automates hypothesis generation and data analysis in biology
summary: Published in Nature, Robin is a multi-agent AI system that integrates literature search agents with data analysis agents to generate hypotheses, propose experiments, interpret results, and refine hypotheses, achieving a semi-autonomous approach to scientific discovery. Applied to dry age-related macular degeneration, Robin identified and helped confirm in vitro efficacy for ripasudil and KL001 as therapeutic candidates.

title: Alibaba unveils Zhenwu M890 AI chip and announces Qwen3.7-Max LLM
summary: Alibaba announced the Zhenwu M890 AI chip, which delivers three times the performance of its predecessor and is described by analysts as a believable replacement for Nvidia's H200 in the Chinese market, though not a true competitor on raw silicon power. The company also revealed that its next-generation AI model, Qwen3.7-Max, would soon be released.

title: JAL deploys Unitree G1 and UBTech Walker E humanoid robots at Haneda Airport
summary: Japan Airlines announced a two-year trial using humanoid robots, including Unitree's G1 and UBTech's Walker E models, at Tokyo's Haneda Airport through a partnership with GMO AI & Robotics. Tasks in the trial include aircraft towing, baggage and cargo loading and unloading, and cabin cleaning, with the experiment scheduled to begin in May 2026 and run through 2028.

title: Hyundai plans 25,000 Atlas robots in factories by 2028
summary: Hyundai Motor Group announced plans to deploy more than 25,000 Boston Dynamics Atlas humanoid robots across Hyundai and Kia manufacturing plants before expanding to external sales, with a U.S. facility operated by Hyundai Mobis set to produce 350,000 actuators annually by 2028.

title: Google launches Gemini 3.5 Flash and announces Gemini Spark at I/O 2026
summary: At Google I/O 2026, Google launched Gemini 3.5 Flash as its strongest agentic and coding model and announced Gemini Spark, a cloud-based proactive AI agent that performs background tasks for users and asks permission before high-stakes actions. Google also unveiled Gemini Omni for video creation and provided updates on AI-powered smart glasses.

title: Boston Dynamics Reveals AI Heavy-Lifting Training for Atlas
summary: Boston Dynamics published details of a reinforcement-learning simulation pipeline that trained Atlas to lift and carry heavy objects, including a mini-fridge, using whole-body coordination and proprioceptive feedback. The company described this as a key capability milestone for factory deployment, demonstrating strength, mobility, and whole-body control for industrial work.

title: Dell AI Factory Reaches 5,000 Enterprise Customers
summary: At Dell Technologies World 2026, Dell announced major expansions to the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, including a new Deskside Agentic AI product, disclosing that more than 5,000 customers are already deploying the platform.

title: Cloudflare and Stripe launch protocol for AI agent commerce
summary: Cloudflare and Stripe launched a protocol that lets AI agents autonomously create cloud accounts, start paid subscriptions, register domains, and deploy applications to production without human dashboard interaction. Stripe handles identity and payment tokenization with a default $100 monthly spending cap per provider, and the capability is available through Stripe Projects, currently in open beta.

title: OpenAI open-sources Symphony agent orchestration framework
summary: OpenAI released Symphony, an agent orchestrator that uses project management tools such as issue trackers as a control plane to coordinate multiple coding agents working autonomously in parallel. Symphony is not a standalone product but a SPEC.md file and reference implementation, built in Elixir, that developers can adapt to their own use cases.

title: Blue Origin Files for 51,600-Satellite Orbital Data Center Fleet
summary: Blue Origin's 'Project Sunrise' filed plans for up to 51,600 satellites in sun-synchronous orbits between 500 and 1,800 km altitude, designed to serve as solar-powered orbital AI data centers.

title: Figure AI robots sort 88,000 packages in 72-hour livestream
summary: Figure AI's F.03 humanoid robots sorted 88,000 packages in 72 continuous hours during a public livestream at its San Jose facility, demonstrating sustained autonomous logistics operation at scale.

title: xAI launches Grok Build, its first terminal-based coding agent
summary: xAI released Grok Build, a terminal-based CLI coding agent currently in early beta, available only to SuperGrok Heavy subscribers. The launch is a late entry into a market defined by Anthropic's Claude Code and expanded by OpenAI's Codex.

title: OpenAI Codex reaches 5 million weekly users, expands into knowledge work
summary: OpenAI reported that Codex, its agentic coding product, has reached 5 million weekly active users, more than six times the level recorded when its desktop app launched in February. Knowledge workers now account for about 20 percent of users and are adopting Codex more than three times as fast as developers, with fast-growing use in data analysis, research, and document creation.

title: Tesla Ends Model S & X Production to Pivot to Optimus Robots
summary: Tesla officially ended production of the Model S and Model X at its Fremont factory on May 10, 2026, holding a ceremony with hundreds of workers to mark the occasion. Tesla stated the move makes way for its Optimus humanoid robot project and autonomous driving technology, with the last units produced as limited edition Plaid-trim send-off models.

title: NASA HPSC AI Chip Unveiled: 500x Faster Than Current Space Computers
summary: NASA unveiled its High Performance Spaceflight Computing (HPSC) chip, developed with Microchip Technology, delivering up to 500 times the processing power of current spacecraft processors. NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory is conducting intense tests on the chip, which packs CPUs, memory, and networking into a single unit designed to enable autonomous onboard decision-making for future deep-space missions.

title: Waymo recalls ~3,800 robotaxis over flood-navigation flaw
summary: Waymo issued a software recall covering its entire fleet of nearly 3,800 fifth- and sixth-generation vehicles after two separate incidents in April in which unoccupied Waymo cars entered floodwaters in San Antonio, including one that was swept into Salado Creek. The company notified NHTSA and said a software remedy is under development, while already modifying vehicle operations to increase weather-related constraints.

title: Colorado Enacts Revised AI Governance Law on May 14, 2026
summary: Colorado's Governor signed Senate Bill 26-189 on May 14, 2026, repealing and replacing the state's original AI Act. The revised law regulates automated decision-making technology used in consequential decisions, removes the prior algorithmic discrimination and duty of care framework, and introduces new consumer rights including meaningful human review following adverse outcomes, with the law set to take effect January 1, 2027.

title: Shield AI and Thunder Tiger Sign MOU to Integrate Hivemind into Taiwan Sea Drones
summary: Shield AI and Taiwan's Thunder Tiger signed a memorandum of understanding to integrate Hivemind autonomy software into Thunder Tiger's unmanned surface vessels, with a live demonstration of an AI-piloted USV planned for summer 2026. The partnership aims to support distributed autonomous coastal defense operations capable of functioning under electronic warfare and GPS disruption.

title: Unitree Unveils World's First Mass-Produced Manned Mecha GD01
summary: Unitree Robotics unveiled the GD01 transformable manned mecha, billed as the world's first mass-produced manned mecha and defined as a civilian vehicle, with a starting price of 3.9 million yuan (~$574,000).

title: Orbital AI data centers face heat rejection as primary engineering constraint
summary: A SpaceDaily analysis argues that orbital data centers cannot use terrestrial air or water cooling, requiring radiator panels for heat rejection, which sets hard limits on chip density, power budgets, and launch mass. Google Research's Project Suncatcher, with TPU-equipped satellite prototypes planned with Planet Labs by early 2027, is cited as a reference point, but the work is framed as a moonshot with open technical questions.

title: Thomson Reuters and Anthropic integrate Claude with CoCounsel Legal via MCP
summary: Thomson Reuters and Anthropic expanded their partnership to connect Claude with CoCounsel Legal through a new MCP integration, allowing legal professionals to move work between Claude and CoCounsel Legal's fiduciary-grade workflows. The next generation of CoCounsel Legal is rebuilt on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK and is expected to reach general availability in summer 2026.

title: Thinking Machines Lab Ships First AI Model
summary: Mira Murati's startup Thinking Machines Lab released its first AI model, processing audio, video, and text in 200-millisecond parallel chunks and targeting real-time interactivity beyond the question-and-answer paradigm of existing voice AI systems.

title: MHI Completes In-Orbit AI Ship Detection Trial with AIRIS
summary: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries completed an in-orbit demonstration of AIRIS (Artificial Intelligence Retraining In Space), successfully detecting ships from maritime satellite imagery using the SOISOC4 space-grade microprocessor developed with JAXA. The system, launched aboard JAXA's RAISE-4 satellite in December 2025, also includes in-orbit testing of the SOISOC4 MPU, with future work focused on ground-based AI retraining and remote onboard updates.

title: Tesla FSD drives 93,000 miles autonomously at Giga Berlin
summary: According to industry observer Sawyer Merritt, Tesla Model Y units at Giga Berlin have self-driven a combined 93,000 miles using Full Self-Driving technology from the production line to the outbound lot, streamlining yard logistics without human drivers.

title: OpenAI Launches $14B Deployment Company with TPG, McKinsey, Goldman, SoftBank
summary: OpenAI launched the Deployment Company on May 11, 2026, a joint venture with a $14 billion post-money valuation backed by 19 private equity and consulting firms, with TPG leading at $4 billion committed capital alongside Advent, Bain Capital, and Brookfield, and McKinsey, Bain and Company, and Capgemini as founding consulting partners. OpenAI simultaneously agreed to acquire Tomoro, an applied AI consulting and engineering firm, bringing approximately 150 Forward Deployed Engineers to embed inside enterprise clients.

title: DeepMind releases AlphaEvolve one-year results
summary: Google DeepMind published one-year performance results for AlphaEvolve, showing a 30% reduction in DNA variant detection errors, an improvement in AC optimal power flow feasible-solution rate from 14% to over 88%, and gains in disaster-risk forecasting and logistics.

title: Institute of Science Tokyo opens fully unmanned humanoid robot lab
summary: The Institute of Science Tokyo opened the Robotics Innovation Center at its Yushima campus, operating with 10 robots including the Maholo LabDroid humanoid and zero on-site human staff. The university plans to expand to around 2,000 robots by 2040 as part of a long-term effort to automate nearly the entire medical research process.

title: OpenAI Launches Daybreak Cyber AI Security Platform
summary: OpenAI launched Daybreak, a cybersecurity initiative combining GPT-5.5 with Trusted Access for Cyber, GPT-5.5-Cyber, and the Codex Security AI agent to create threat models, validate vulnerabilities, and automate detection of high-risk attack paths. OpenAI says it is working with industry and government partners as it prepares to deploy increasingly more cyber-capable models.

title: Ukraine Deploys AI-Controlled Turrets to Intercept Drones
summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defense confirmed combat deployment of an AI-controlled anti-drone turret developed under the Brave1 platform, using fiber optics to detect and shoot down enemy drones in live battlefield conditions.

title: Kodiak & Roehl begin autonomous freight ops Dallas-Houston
summary: Kodiak Robotics and Roehl Transport launched commercial autonomous freight operations on the Dallas-to-Houston corridor, with trucks equipped with the Kodiak Driver hauling freight four times roundtrip per week. Kodiak noted it continues working toward fully driverless operations by the end of 2026.

title: Australian Researchers Deploy NASA/IBM Prithvi AI Model on Two Satellites in Orbit
summary: A team of Australian researchers successfully uploaded and demonstrated the open-source Prithvi Geospatial AI foundation model on two in-orbit platforms, the Kanyini Satellite and the ISS-mounted IMAGIN-e payload, marking the first geospatial foundation model deployed in orbit. The model, trained by NASA and IBM on 13 years of geospatial data, was evaluated for flood and cloud detection across both platforms.

title: Vancouver City Council Approves Delivery Robot Pilot on Sidewalks
summary: Vancouver's city council voted to approve a pilot project allowing Serve Robotics' autonomous food delivery robots to operate on sidewalks in Kitsilano and Downtown neighbourhoods, with the rollout expected this fall. The vote passed despite concerns raised about accessibility, pedestrian safety, and the impact on gig workers.
