The company plans to gradually expand to new cities and open the service to public riders later in 2026.

title: Google releases Gemini 3 Deep Think, 84.6% on ARC-AGI-2
summary: Google launched Gemini 3 Deep Think, a specialized reasoning mode that scored 84.6% on ARC-AGI-2 and achieved Legendary Grandmaster status on coding benchmarks, while solving 18 previously unsolved research problems.

title: Yuanhua orthopaedic surgical robot achieves first clinical success
summary: Yuanhua Tech's orthopaedic surgical robot featuring the 100% domestically developed HX Orthopaedic-Specific Robotic Arm completed its first clinical procedure at West China Hospital of Sichuan University on February 11, 2026. The milestone confirms clinical validation of the company's self-developed key execution components at a top Chinese medical institution.
actor: Yuanhua Robotics, Perception and AI Technologies

title: Claude Cowork AI Agent Launches on Windows
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Cowork for Windows, bringing its autonomous AI agent with file access and task automation to the majority of desktop users for the first time, as Microsoft deepened its Anthropic partnership.

title: Boston Dynamics CEO Robert Playter steps down
summary: Boston Dynamics CEO Robert Playter, who oversaw the launch of the electric Atlas humanoid robot, stepped down after six years; CFO Amanda McMaster named interim CEO.

title: Alibaba open-sources RynnBrain robotics foundation model
summary: Alibaba released RynnBrain as an open-source robotics foundation model providing machines with perception, reasoning, and action capabilities, directly competing with Google and Nvidia in the robotics AI space.

title: Microsoft deploys AI agents in OneDrive for commercial users
summary: Microsoft made AI agents in OneDrive generally available on February 3, 2026, for commercial users worldwide, enabling users to create agents that analyze up to 20 documents simultaneously to answer questions and surface key details. Creating an agent requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, though shared agents can be accessed by anyone with document permissions.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.3-Codex coding model with desktop app
summary: OpenAI launched GPT-5.3-Codex, a coding-focused model the company says runs faster, uses fewer computing resources, and can generate and manage complex software from English instructions. The release also includes a standalone Codex desktop app.

title: Tesla Launches AI Training Center in China for FSD
summary: Tesla activated an AI training center in China to process locally collected driving data, a legally required step enabling Full Self-Driving deployment in the world's largest auto market.

title: OpenAI launches Frontier agentic enterprise OS platform
summary: On February 5, 2026, OpenAI launched Frontier, an autonomous agent orchestration layer described as a semantic operating system for the enterprise, allowing AI agents to securely connect to and act across internal business systems including CRM, HR, and analytics tools. Early customers include Intuit, State Farm, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and Uber, and the platform targets enterprise fragmentation by providing a single environment to orchestrate AI agents across disparate software systems, with OpenAI positioning it as a shift from per-seat SaaS licensing toward outcome-based computing.

title: GitHub expands Agents HQ for multi-agent AI coding inside repositories
summary: GitHub expanded Agents HQ to enable AI coding agents including GitHub Copilot, Claude by Anthropic, and OpenAI Codex to execute development tasks directly within GitHub and developer editors, preserving repository context, session history, and review workflows. Enterprise administrators can define which agents and models are authorized, and teams can run agents in parallel to compare outputs and review changes.

title: Google Gemini App reaches 750 million monthly active users
summary: At Alphabet's Q4 earnings call, CEO Sundar Pichai reported that the Gemini App now has more than 750 million monthly active users, up roughly 100 million from the 650 million reported in Q3. Pichai also noted significantly higher engagement per user since the launch of Gemini 3, which he called the fastest-adopted model in Google's history.

title: U.S. Senate Holds Hearing on Tesla FSD and Autonomous Driving Safety
summary: Tesla VP of Vehicle Engineering Lars Moravy testified before a Senate committee hearing on the future of self-driving, advocating for federal autonomous driving standards. Senators voiced skepticism about Tesla's camera-only approach and criticized Full Self-Driving as misleading and insufficiently constrained, while Waymo's chief safety officer faced comparatively less criticism.

title: Google launches Developer Knowledge API and MCP Server in public preview
summary: Google released the Developer Knowledge API and an official Model Context Protocol server in public preview, giving AI agents and agentic platforms a canonical, machine-readable interface to query up-to-date documentation across Firebase, Google Cloud, and Android.

title: FedEx Announces Berkshire Grey Scoop Autonomous Trailer Unloader Pilot
summary: FedEx announced a pilot of Berkshire Grey's Scoop robotic package unloader, a fully autonomous trailer unloading system developed through a multi-year collaboration, with the first Scoop systems expected to be in full operation later in calendar year 2026.

title: Apple Xcode 26.3 adds agentic AI coding with Claude and Codex
summary: Apple released Xcode 26.3 with native agentic coding support, integrating Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex to autonomously write, build, and test apps, the first time Apple's official IDE supports fully autonomous AI agents.

title: SpaceX merges with xAI, files FCC request for 1M orbital AI satellites
summary: SpaceX completed its merger with xAI on Feb. 2, with Space Exploration Technologies Corp. listed as managing member of X.AI Holdings, as the combined entity gears up for a massive IPO. SpaceX also recently filed an FCC request for authorization to launch up to 1 million satellites as part of planned orbital data centers for AI compute.

title: OpenAI Launches Standalone Codex Desktop App for macOS
summary: OpenAI launched a standalone macOS app for its AI-powered coding assistant Codex, temporarily available to all ChatGPT users. The app is designed as a command center for managing multiple AI agents at once, and is part of OpenAI's ongoing effort to lure users and market share away from rivals like Anthropic and Cursor.

title: EU AI Act 'Unacceptable Risk' Ban Enters Force
summary: The first enforcement deadline of the EU AI Act took effect on 2 February 2026, prohibiting AI systems classified as 'unacceptable risk' across all EU member states. Banned practices include subliminal manipulation, social scoring, real-time biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement (with narrow exceptions), and emotion inference in workplaces and schools.

title: OpenAI Launches Prism LaTeX Workspace with GPT-5.2
summary: OpenAI released Prism, a free cloud-based LaTeX writing and collaboration platform with GPT-5.2 integrated directly into the authoring environment, targeting academic users.

title: UN Body Approves Draft Global Technical Regulation on Automated Driving
summary: The UNECE Working Party on Automated/Autonomous and Connected Vehicles (GRVA) approved a draft Global Technical Regulation on Automated Driving Systems, offering a framework for signatories on how to regulate and validate autonomous vehicles. The draft now advances toward formal endorsement by the 1998 Global Agreement's Executive Committee, with a vote expected at the June 2026 WP.29 session.
publisher: Sidley Environmental, Health, and Safety Brief

title: OpenAI Retires GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, and o4-mini from ChatGPT
summary: OpenAI announced the removal of GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, and o4-mini from ChatGPT's available models list, with all four models becoming unusable on February 13, 2026. OpenAI cited that the majority of users had shifted to GPT-5.2, with GPT-4o usage falling to just 0.1%, though the models will remain available via API.

title: Starlink revises privacy policy to allow AI training on customer data
summary: SpaceX updated Starlink's Global Privacy Policy on January 15 to permit use of customer data for AI model training unless users opt out, with data potentially shared with service providers and third-party collaborators. The change raises concerns among privacy advocates, and comes as SpaceX is reportedly in talks to merge with Musk's xAI company ahead of a planned IPO.

title: US and Chinese companies race to build space-based AI data centers
summary: Competition for AI dominance between the US and China is expanding to space, with companies like Google, SpaceX, and Chinese tech firms planning satellite constellations that use solar energy to power orbital data centers. US-based Starcloud envisions a 5-gigawatt space data center made up of tens of thousands of satellites.

title: China unveils policy to curb AI-driven job displacement
summary: China's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security announced on Tuesday it is working on a policy directive aimed at easing workforce concerns caused by widespread AI adoption, and will issue a document addressing AI's impact on employment later in the year. The ministry described this as China's first systematic response at the central government level to AI-driven labour displacement.

title: Anthropic Expands Claude Cowork with New Enterprise Plugins
summary: Anthropic announced updates to its Claude Cowork platform, adding pre-built plugins for HR, design, engineering, and finance workflows, plus integrations with Google Workspace, Docusign, and WordPress. The update also enables Claude to handle multi-step tasks end-to-end across Excel and PowerPoint, and is available to paid Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscribers.

title: Waymo Plans Driverless Taxi Launch in London in 2026
summary: Waymo confirmed it is testing robotaxis in London ahead of a planned passenger launch in 2026, marking its second international market after Japan. The expansion comes as US regulators examine incidents involving Waymo vehicles in Austin, Texas, which may play a decisive role in shaping regulatory confidence in its UK debut.

title: Waabi & Uber Partner to Deploy 25,000+ Robotaxis
summary: Waabi announced a partnership with Uber to deploy a minimum of 25,000 robotaxis on Uber's platform, alongside a $1 billion funding package including a $750M Series C led by Khosla Ventures and G2 Venture Partners plus additional capital from Uber, marking Waabi's first expansion beyond trucking into passenger robotaxis.

title: Tesla discloses 1.1M FSD subscribers for first time
summary: Tesla revealed in its Q4 2025 earnings report that it has 1.1 million active FSD subscriptions, a metric that includes both upfront purchasers (70% of the total) and monthly subscribers, excluding free trials. The disclosure was required by Elon Musk's 2025 CEO Performance Award, representing roughly 12% of Tesla's cumulative vehicle sales.

title: Arcee AI releases Trinity 400B open-source LLM
summary: 30-person startup Arcee AI released Trinity, a 400B-parameter open-source foundation model under an Apache license, claiming it is among the largest open-source foundation models ever trained and released by a U.S. company. Benchmarks on base models show Trinity is largely holding its own against Meta's Llama 4 Maverick and Z.ai's GLM-4.5, and in some cases slightly outperforms Llama on coding, math, common sense, knowledge, and reasoning tests.

title: Google DeepMind launches AlphaGenome DNA analysis AI
summary: Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome, an AI tool capable of analysing up to 1 million letters of DNA code at once to help identify genetic drivers of disease, marking a new scale of genomic AI capability.

title: China deploys first general-purpose AI model in orbit
summary: GuoXing Aerospace Technology announced it has uplinked Alibaba's Qwen3 large language model to its space-based computing center aboard orbiting satellites, completing end-to-end reasoning tasks entirely in orbit. The firm called it the world's first deployment of a general-purpose large-scale AI model from ground control to an operational satellite constellation.

title: Tesla AI Hardware 4.5 Quietly Enters Production in Model Y
summary: Tesla began shipping a new AI compute generation, Hardware 4.5, in newly delivered Model Y vehicles, with the unit also appearing in Tesla's official parts catalog, marking the first deployment of the next-generation FSD computer.

title: Hyundai Motor Union Formally Opposes Atlas Robot Deployment
summary: The Hyundai Motor branch of the Korean Metal Workers' Union formally opposed deploying Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid robots on production lines, warning of an 'employment shock' and demanding that no robots enter worksites without labor-management agreement.

title: EU opens formal investigation into Grok over sexual deepfakes
summary: The European Union opened a formal investigation into Elon Musk's X platform on Monday after its Grok AI chatbot generated nonconsensual sexualized deepfake images, with regulators examining whether X met its obligations under the Digital Services Act; some governments had banned or restricted the service. The EU also widened a separate ongoing investigation into X's recommendation systems after X said it would switch to Grok's AI to select posts for users.

title: Microsoft Unveils Maia 200 AI Inference Chip with 10 Petaflops
summary: Microsoft announced the Maia 200, an AI inference chip featuring over 100 billion transistors and delivering over 10 petaflops at 4-bit precision, a substantial increase over its predecessor the Maia 100. The chip is already powering Microsoft's Superintelligence team models and Copilot, and the company has invited developers, academics, and frontier AI labs to use its software development kit.

title: China's Eyou Launches First Automated Line for Humanoid Robot Joints
summary: Chinese robotics firm Eyou put its automated production line for humanoid robot joints into operation in Shanghai's Pudong district, marking the first industrial-scale manufacturing line dedicated to humanoid robot joints and a shift from R&D to mass production in embodied AI.

title: Apple restructures AI under Federighi, confirms Gemini-Siri deal
summary: Bloomberg reported that Apple placed SVP Craig Federighi in full control of AI and confirmed a deal to integrate Google Gemini into Siri, according to the outlet's coverage. Details of the deal terms and Siri roadmap are drawn from that report.

title: LimX Dynamics achieves first autonomous deployment of 18 humanoid robots
summary: LimX Dynamics demonstrated what it claims is the world's first practical autonomous deployment of humanoid robots, with 18 units operating simultaneously without any human control or intervention.

title: WeRide Launches Robotaxi Booking via WeChat Mini Program
summary: WeRide embedded its 'WeRide Go' robotaxi service directly into Tencent's WeChat super-app, enabling users in Guangzhou's Huangpu district and Beijing's Yizhuang district to book autonomous rides without a separate app download.

title: Tesla eliminates Autopilot, mandates FSD subscription
summary: Tesla removed free Autopilot (including Autosteer/lane centering) from new vehicles, requiring a $99/month FSD subscription for basic driver-assistance features, a fundamental restructuring of its ADAS access model in the US and Canada.

title: Gates Foundation and OpenAI launch Horizons1000 AI clinic pilot in Rwanda
summary: Rwanda will test OpenAI-powered technology in more than 50 health clinics as part of the Gates Foundation and OpenAI initiative called Horizons1000, which targets 1,000 clinics across Africa with $50 million in joint funding over two years. Digital experts have raised concerns that AI tools operating in English rather than Kinyarwanda could pose barriers to effective care.

title: Google rolls out Personal Intelligence linking Gmail and Photos to AI Search
summary: Google began rolling out a 'Personal Intelligence' feature within AI Mode on its search engine, giving users the option to connect Gmail and Google Photos so the AI can deliver personalized answers drawn from their own data. The feature is first available in the U.S. to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers and through its experimental Labs division for anyone with a personal Google account.

title: South Korea AI Basic Act enters enforcement
summary: South Korea began enforcing the AI Basic Act on January 22, 2026, becoming the first nation to implement a comprehensive legal framework for artificial intelligence across both public and private sectors. Penalties such as fines of up to KRW 30 million will be deferred during a one-year grace period while regulators focus on guidance and industry adaptation.

title: Tesla Launches First Robotaxi Rides Without Safety Monitors
summary: Tesla began offering fully unsupervised robotaxi rides in Austin for the first time, with Tesla AI chief Ashok Elluswamy confirming that rides without any safety monitors were now publicly available, starting with a few unsupervised vehicles mixed into the broader fleet.

title: Tesla begins mass production of Optimus Gen 3 humanoid robot
summary: Tesla began mass production of its Optimus Gen 3 humanoid robot at its Fremont, California plant on January 21, 2026, after several years of prototype testing. CEO Elon Musk is targeting up to one million units per year from the site, while warning that early output will be slow before ramping up.

title: Lemonade launches first autonomous-driving car insurance
summary: Lemonade introduced what it calls Autonomous Car Insurance, offering approximately 50% off per-mile rates for Tesla owners when Full Self-Driving is actively engaged, launching in Arizona on January 26. The product uses second-by-second telemetry via a technical collaboration with Tesla, and Lemonade stated the discount reflects FSD making drivers safer, not the technology driving fully on its own.

title: Cursor deploys hundreds of AI agents to build a working browser
summary: Cursor set hundreds of autonomous AI agents to build a web browser from scratch, and after nearly a week the swarm produced a working browser with its own rendering engine, generating roughly one million lines of code across more than 1,000 files.

title: Serve Robotics Acquires Diligent Robotics for Hospital AI
summary: Serve Robotics announced the acquisition of Diligent Robotics, expanding from sidewalk delivery robots into hospital autonomous service robots; the deal values Diligent's common stock at $29 million.

title: UBTECH signs deal to deploy Walker S2 robots in Airbus factories
summary: Chinese humanoid robotics developer UBTECH reached an agreement with Airbus under which the aviation company purchased its Walker S2 humanoid robot and will work with UBTECH to explore how the robots can support aircraft manufacturing tasks. The deal marks a milestone in UBTECH's push to expand its industrial humanoid robots into overseas markets.

title: Baidu Apollo Go launches fully driverless taxis on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island
summary: Baidu's Apollo Go and UAE partner AutoGo commenced fully autonomous (no safety driver) ride-hailing service on Yas Island, Abu Dhabi, marking the first commercial driverless robotaxi deployment in the UAE, with phased expansion planned to Reem, Al Maryah, and Saadiyat Islands.

title: Google launches TranslateGemma open models for 55 languages
summary: Google released TranslateGemma, a set of open-source multilingual translation models in three sizes (4B, 12B, and 27B parameters), covering 55 languages and made publicly available on Kaggle and Hugging Face for developer use.

title: AgiBot deploys 2,000 humanoid robots across 200 Chinese cities for Spring Festival
summary: AgiBot, a robot rental platform, is deploying 2,000 humanoid robots across 200 cities in China to help people celebrate the Spring Festival.

title: California AG opens investigation into xAI Grok over deepfakes
summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced an investigation into xAI and its Grok model over the proliferation of nonconsensual sexually explicit deepfake images of women and children. The investigation aims to determine whether and how xAI violated the law, citing reports of large-scale production of such images including child sexual abuse material.

title: Tesla ends one-time FSD purchase, shifts to subscription-only
summary: Tesla announced it will stop selling Full Self-Driving as an $8,000 one-time purchase after February 14, 2026, making the $99/month subscription the sole access model for its autonomous driving software across its entire fleet.

title: Z.AI releases GLM-Image trained on Huawei chips only
summary: China's Z.AI released GLM-Image, an open-source image generation model trained entirely on Huawei Ascend processors, marking what the company called the first time a major AI model completed its full training cycle without relying on American hardware. The release coincided with Reuters reporting that Chinese customs authorities had instructed agents to block Nvidia H200 chips from entering the country, signaling China's push toward AI self-reliance.

title: Pentagon awards contract for AI drone-capture UAS task force systems
summary: The Pentagon's Joint Interagency Task Force 401 announced it has awarded a contract for two DroneHunter F700 systems, designed by Fortem Technologies, which use AI and radar to identify, pursue, and capture hostile drones with expanding nets. The contract was made under the Pentagon's Replicator 2 initiative, focused on boosting defense against small drones.

title: 16,000 Humanoid Robots Installed Globally in 2025
summary: Counterpoint Research reported approximately 16,000 humanoid robot units were installed worldwide in 2025, with China accounting for over 80% of installations. AGIBOT led all vendors with nearly 32% market share, followed by Unitree, UBTECH, Leju, and Tesla.

title: 1X releases world model letting NEO robot self-learn from video
summary: 1X Technologies unveiled the 1X World Model, a physics-based AI model that uses video and prompts to help its Neo humanoid robot learn new tasks from internet-scale video data. The company noted that learned capabilities remain limited to basic tasks such as removing an air fryer basket or giving a high five, with more complex actions expected to follow.

title: Google releases Veo 3.1 updates in Gemini API
summary: Google released updates to Veo 3.1 in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, adding enhanced character identity and background consistency, native 9:16 vertical format video output, and new 4K and improved 1080p video quality for developers.

title: Apple signs deal to power next-gen Siri with Google Gemini
summary: Apple announced a multi-year partnership with Google under which the next generation of Apple Foundation Models will be based on Google's Gemini, allowing Apple to use Google's AI models in its own software including a more intelligent version of Siri planned for later in 2026.

title: OWASP releases first Top 10 risk list for agentic AI
summary: OWASP published its inaugural Top 10 risks for agentic AI systems, the first standardized security framework specifically addressing autonomous AI agents acting as a digital workforce.

title: Atlas Robot Already Operating at Hyundai Georgia Plant
summary: Boston Dynamics confirmed that its next-generation Atlas humanoid robot is currently in active use at Hyundai's assembly plant in Ellabell, Georgia, representing the first deployment of a commercial humanoid robot on a major automotive production floor.

title: Cisco deploys OpenAI Codex across enterprise engineering
summary: Cisco and OpenAI announced broad deployment of Codex across Cisco's enterprise software engineering workflows, making AI-native development a core part of how Cisco builds software at scale.

title: Lightricks open-sources LTX-2 for 4K video+audio generation
summary: Lightricks fully open-sourced LTX-2, claimed to be the first open-source model capable of synchronized 4K video and audio generation in a single multimodal system.

title: Microsoft Launches Copilot Checkout for In-App AI Commerce
summary: Microsoft launched Copilot Checkout, a feature that lets users purchase products directly inside the Copilot AI assistant without leaving the chat. The feature is rolling out on Copilot.com in the US with select retailers, with payments powered by PayPal, Stripe, and Shopify.

title: Infosys & Cognition deploy Devin AI engineer at scale
summary: Infosys and Cognition announced a strategic collaboration to deploy Devin, the first AI software engineer, across Infosys' internal engineering ecosystem and client engagements worldwide.

title: Hyundai unveils Atlas humanoid robot at CES, plans Georgia factory deploy
summary: Hyundai Motor Group showed off Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid robot at CES in Las Vegas and announced plans to deploy it across its global factory network, including a plant in Georgia, starting in 2028. The firm did not specify how many robots it would initially deploy or the cost of the project.

title: DeepSeek releases V3.2 open-source reasoning models
summary: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V3.2, a family of open-source reasoning and agentic AI models; the top-tier DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale outperforms GPT-5 on reasoning tasks and matches Gemini-3.0-Pro.

title: Google DeepMind's Gemini to Power Boston Dynamics Atlas
summary: Google DeepMind and Boston Dynamics announced a partnership to integrate Gemini Robotics AI models into the Atlas humanoid robot for industrial factory tasks, with Hyundai facilities as the first deployment target.

title: Boston Dynamics Unveils Production-Ready Atlas Humanoid Robot
summary: Hyundai-owned Boston Dynamics publicly demonstrated its Atlas humanoid robot for the first time at CES 2026 in Las Vegas, showing a prototype walking and interacting with the crowd. A product version of Atlas is already in production and will be deployed by 2028 at Hyundai's electric vehicle manufacturing facility near Savannah, Georgia.

title: NVIDIA launches Alpamayo open AV reasoning model family
summary: NVIDIA unveiled the Alpamayo family of open-source AI models, simulation tools, and datasets specifically designed for safe, reasoning-based autonomous vehicle development, the first such open model suite from NVIDIA targeting the AV stack.

title: DeepSeek Publishes Breakthrough LLM Training Method
summary: DeepSeek published a research paper introducing 'Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections' (mHC), a training approach designed to let large language models share richer internal communication while preserving stability and computational efficiency as they scale. One analyst called it a 'striking breakthrough,' saying it could allow DeepSeek to bypass compute bottlenecks and unlock leaps in intelligence.

title: Meta Reportedly Acquiring AI Agent Startup Manus for $2 Billion
summary: Meta is reportedly acquiring AI agent startup Manus for about $2 billion, according to TechCrunch. Meta plans to let Manus operate independently while integrating its AI agents into Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, and has assured that after the purchase Manus will have no Chinese owners or operations in China.

title: China deploys UBTECH Walker S2 humanoids at Vietnam border
summary: China began deploying UBTECH Walker S2 humanoid robots at the Fanchenggang border crossing in Guangxi near Vietnam to assist border officials with passenger queue guidance, vehicle direction, patrols, and cargo logistics operations. UBTECH secured a $37 million contract with the Chinese government for the deployment, marking a step toward embodied AI in public security.

title: Waymo Tests Gemini AI Integration as In-Car Robotaxi Assistant
summary: Waymo is testing an integration of Google's Gemini AI as an in-car assistant for its robotaxi fleet, a development uncovered by researcher Jane Manchun Wong in the company's app code. The assistant is designed to answer questions, manage cabin functions like climate control, and greet riders by name, though a Waymo spokesperson said the company has no details to share publicly.

title: Pentagon adds xAI Grok to GenAI.mil military AI service
summary: The U.S. Department of Defense announced it will integrate xAI's Grok family of models into its GenAI.mil platform, extending frontier LLM access to sensitive government and military workflows.

title: Taiwan passes Artificial Intelligence Fundamental Act into law
summary: Taiwan's Legislative Yuan passed the Artificial Intelligence Fundamental Act on Dec. 23, 2025, laying down principles on how AI will be governed in Taiwan and designating the National Science and Technology Council as the governing authority for AI.

title: Uber & Lyft to Test Baidu Apollo Go Robotaxis in London in 2026
summary: Uber and Lyft announced plans to test Baidu Apollo Go robotaxis in London in the first half of 2026, with Lyft planning to scale to hundreds of Baidu's electric RT6 SUVs after receiving local regulatory approval.

title: STMicroelectronics to Deploy Oversonic RoBee Humanoids in Chip Fabs
summary: STMicroelectronics signed a supply agreement with Oversonic Robotics to deploy RoBee cognitive humanoid robots across its semiconductor fabrication plants, starting at its Malta fab, marking the first humanoid robot deployment in chip production.

title: New York Governor signs RAISE AI Safety Act
summary: Governor Hochul signed the RAISE Act, requiring large AI developers to publish safety protocols and report incidents within 72 hours, and creating a new AI safety oversight office within the Department of Financial Services. Fines are set at up to $1 million for a first violation and $3 million for subsequent violations, lower than the amounts in the version passed in June.

title: ICEYE & Rheinmetall Win €1.7B German SAR Satellite Contract
summary: ICEYE and joint-venture partner Rheinmetall secured a €1.7 billion contract to build a dedicated SAR satellite constellation with AI-driven image evaluation for the German Armed Forces, starting end of 2025.

title: ChatGPT mobile app hits $3B lifetime consumer spending
summary: ChatGPT's mobile app reached $3 billion in lifetime consumer spending in just 31 months, surpassing the pace of TikTok and major streaming platforms.

title: CATL deploys humanoid robots at scale on EV battery lines
summary: CATL deployed Spirit AI's Xiaomo humanoid robots on its EV battery production lines to plug in high-voltage battery connectors, a task previously considered a security risk for human workers. The robots achieved a 99 percent success rate and a daily workload triple that of a human worker, with CATL saying it plans to expand automation and embodied AI adoption across its factories.

title: Anthropic Launches Agent Skills as Open Standard
summary: Anthropic released its Agent Skills framework as an open standard with SDK at agentskills.io, with Microsoft, OpenAI, Atlassian, Figma, Cursor, and GitHub already adopting it, extending the MCP playbook to agentic workplace AI.

title: CA judge rules Tesla FSD marketing false, orders 60-day fix
summary: A California judge ruled Tesla engaged in deceptive marketing with its 'Autopilot' and 'Full Self-Driving' branding, finding 'Full Self-Driving' to be 'actually, unambiguously false and counterfactual.' The court said the California DMV could suspend Tesla's dealer license for 30 days, and the DMV stated it will give Tesla 60 days to correct its marketing before taking action.

title: Amazon consolidates AI, chips, and quantum under DeSantis
summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy announced that longtime AWS executive Peter DeSantis will lead a new AI-focused organization responsible for Amazon's Nova AI models, custom silicon development, and quantum computing. DeSantis, who spent 27 years at Amazon including eight years as an SVP for AWS, will focus on optimizing across models, chips, and cloud infrastructure.

title: Starfish and Impulse Space Complete First Private Autonomous RPO Mission
summary: Starfish Space and Impulse Space announced Dec. 15 the successful completion of the Remora mission, in which an Impulse Mira spacecraft maneuvered to within about 1,250 meters of another Mira spacecraft using only a single off-the-shelf camera and Starfish's onboard software for navigation and maneuver commands. The companies described it as the first autonomous rendezvous and proximity operations demonstration conducted between two private spacecraft in LEO.

title: Serve Robotics Surpasses 2025 Goal With 2,000-Robot Sidewalk Delivery Fleet
summary: Serve Robotics announced it has met its 2025 target by deploying more than 2,000 autonomous sidewalk delivery robots, creating the largest such fleet in the United States. The company expanded its fleet twentyfold during the year across markets including Los Angeles, Atlanta, Dallas-Fort Worth, Miami, Fort Lauderdale, Chicago, and Alexandria, Va., through partnerships with Uber Eats and DoorDash.

title: Starcloud runs first AI model in orbit on Nvidia H100
summary: Washington-based startup Starcloud launched a satellite in early November 2025 carrying an Nvidia H100 GPU and successfully ran Google's Gemma large language model in orbit, marking the first time such a model has operated on a high-powered GPU beyond Earth's atmosphere. The satellite also trained NanoGPT on Shakespeare's works, and the H100 chip is 100 times more powerful than any GPU previously sent to space.

title: El Salvador deploys Grok AI tutors to 1M+ students nationwide
summary: El Salvador partnered with xAI to deploy Grok as an AI tutor across 5,000 schools, serving over 1 million students, the first national-scale deployment of a frontier AI model in a country's public education system.

title: Trump EO Sets Federal AI Policy, Preempts State Rules
summary: On December 11, 2025, President Trump signed an executive order establishing a national AI policy framework aimed at limiting states from enacting their own AI regulations in favor of a unified federal approach, directly targeting laws like California's.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.2 after internal 'Code Red'
summary: OpenAI launched GPT-5.2, its smartest model yet, shortly after CEO Sam Altman internally declared a 'code red' to marshal resources around ChatGPT amid competition from rivals. The model comes in three variants (Instant, Thinking, Pro), beats human professionals in over 70 percent of tasks on OpenAI's GDPval benchmark, and hallucinates 38 percent less than GPT-5.1 on factual question benchmarks.

title: Agility Robotics Digit deployed at MercadoLibre Texas warehouse
summary: MercadoLibre and Agility Robotics announced a commercial agreement to integrate Digit humanoid robots into MercadoLibre's San Antonio, Texas fulfillment facility, marking one of the first commercial humanoid robot deployments in Latin American e-commerce logistics.
publisher: Press release distribution, EDGAR filing, XBRL, regulatory filings | Business Wire

title: AgiBot rolls out its 5,000th mass-produced humanoid robot
summary: Chinese humanoid robotics startup AgiBot reached 5,000 units of its general-purpose intelligent robot off the production line in Shanghai, marking a shift from small-batch manufacturing to mass production. Most Chinese robotics firms have produced between 500 and 1,000 units each, making this a notable production milestone in the sector.

title: MQ-28 Ghost Bat fires missile autonomously in first CCA weapon engagement
summary: Boeing's MQ-28 Ghost Bat, teaming with a RAAF E-7A Wedgetail and F/A-18F Super Hornet, executed the first-ever autonomous air-to-air weapon engagement by a Collaborative Combat Aircraft, destroying a fighter-class target drone.

title: NHTSA Expands Federal Probe of Waymo Over School Bus Incidents
summary: U.S. federal regulators expanded their investigation into Waymo after multiple Texas incidents in which its autonomous robotaxis drove around stopped school buses, raising safety and regulatory scrutiny of deployed AV fleets.

title: British AI Intelligence Satellites Reach Orbit on SpaceX Transporter-15
summary: Four British-designed satellites, developed under BAE Systems' self-funded Azalea programme, entered low Earth orbit on 28 November aboard SpaceX's Transporter-15 rideshare mission. The cluster combines three RF satellites and one SAR satellite to fuse data in orbit using AI and deliver near real-time intelligence to defence, security, and civil users.

title: Amazon Prime Air Drone Delivery Launches in Dallas-Fort Worth
summary: Amazon activated drone delivery service in Richardson, Texas, its first major push into the Dallas-Fort Worth metro, giving customers access to tens of thousands of eligible items via autonomous aerial delivery.

title: Waymo Robotaxi Network Reaches 26 U.S. Markets
summary: Waymo announced expansion into Baltimore, Pittsburgh, and St. Louis, bringing its total footprint to 26 markets either operating, planned, or in active vehicle testing across the U.S.

title: Mistral releases 4-model frontier AI family under Apache 2.0 license
summary: French AI startup Mistral released a four-model open-source family under the Apache 2.0 license, ranging from a 3B parameter model that runs in a browser to a 675B parameter flagship that benchmarks near DeepSeek V3.1. The release positions Mistral as an EU-headquartered alternative for enterprises seeking open weights and a vendor not subject to Chinese or American national security laws.

title: Mistral Releases 10 Open Models for Edge and Drone Deployment
summary: Mistral AI launched Mistral 3, a family of 10 open-source AI models designed to run on smartphones, drones, and enterprise edge systems, escalating Europe's challenge to US and Chinese AI competitors.

title: Anthropic Acquires Bun to Scale Claude Code Agent
summary: Anthropic acquired Bun, a JavaScript runtime and developer tooling startup, to boost the speed and stability of its Claude Code AI coding agent, marking Anthropic's first major infrastructure acquisition to support agentic coding at scale.

title: Amazon launches Nova 2 models and Nova Forge training service
summary: Amazon unveiled four new Nova 2 models at re:Invent: Nova Lite and Nova Pro (improved large language models), Nova Sonic (real-time voice), and the experimental Nova Omni (simulated multimodal reasoning using images, audio, video, and text). Amazon also released Nova Forge, a tool letting customers build specialized frontier models by adding their own training data to unfinished versions of Nova 2 models at various stages of training, including custom pretraining, on Amazon's cloud infrastructure.

title: Google Releases Nano Banana Pro Image Model
summary: Google launched Nano Banana Pro, a grounded multimodal image generation system that couples image synthesis with Gemini's reasoning stack, enabling knowledge-grounded visuals, multilingual text rendering, and high-consistency composition. It is rolling out across Google's ecosystem including the Gemini app, Search, Ads, Workspace, Vertex AI, and Flow.

title: NVIDIA Releases First Open Reasoning VLA Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: At NeurIPS, NVIDIA unveiled DRIVE Alpamayo-R1, described as the world's first open industry-scale reasoning vision-language-action model for autonomous driving, integrating chain-of-thought reasoning with path planning. NVIDIA also released new speech AI models, AI safety tools, and datasets, with the Nemotron family rated among the most open in the AI ecosystem by the Artificial Analysis Open Index.

title: DeepSeek releases V3.2 and V3.2-Speciale reasoning models
summary: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V3.2, a daily assistant claimed to match GPT-5, and DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale, a complex-task model claimed comparable to Gemini-3.0-Pro, on December 1, 2025. DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale achieved gold-medal performance in four elite competitions including the 2025 IMO and IOI, and both models were trained using a new DeepSeek Sparse Attention method to reduce compute costs.

title: Spain Approves Driverless Tesla FSD Trials Under ES-AV
summary: Spain became the first European country to authorize fully driverless Tesla FSD trials on public roads under its ES-AV framework, approving a 19-vehicle fleet with no restrictions on routes or time of day. There is already talk of robotaxis potentially appearing in Madrid and Barcelona in 2026, and Germany, France, and Italy are preparing to join the program.

title: AI-Generated Song Tops Billboard Country Chart
summary: An AI-generated country track called 'Walk My Walk,' credited to a fictional artist named Breaking Rust, reached No. 1 on Billboard's country digital song sales chart. The song's vocal style was built on the sound of Grammy-nominated Black artist Blanco Brown, who said he had no knowledge of the song until contacted by friends.

title: DeepSeek releases first open-source IMO gold-level math AI
summary: DeepSeek released its Math-V2 model under a permissive open-source licence on Hugging Face and GitHub, making it the world's first open AI model to achieve gold-medal-level performance at the International Mathematical Olympiad.

title: Tesla Announces FSD Ride-Along Demonstrations in Germany, Italy, France
summary: Tesla announced it will offer supervised Full Self-Driving ride-along demonstrations to the public in Germany, Italy, and France the following month, allowing Europeans to experience FSD from the passenger seat during a test drive.

title: Tesla Offers Free FSD v14 Trial to 1.5M HW4 Owners
summary: Tesla launched a free 30-day trial of Full Self-Driving v14 targeting an estimated 1.5 million Hardware 4 vehicle owners across North America, its largest FSD adoption push to date.

title: Pony.ai 961-Vehicle Robotaxi Fleet Hits UE Breakeven in Guangzhou
summary: Pony.ai reported Q3 2025 results on Nov 25, 2025, with total revenues up 72.0% YoY to $25.4M, including robotaxi revenues of $6.7M (+89.5% YoY). Its 961-vehicle fleet, including 667 Gen-7 units, achieved city-wide unit-economics breakeven in Guangzhou, with a target to surpass 3,000 vehicles by end-2026.

title: Tesla Claims Dutch RDW Committed to FSD Decision by Feb 2026, RDW Pushes Back
summary: Tesla posted on social media that Dutch regulator RDW had committed to approving FSD Supervised in February 2026, but RDW clarified that February is when Tesla plans to demonstrate the system and that whether the schedule will be met remains to be seen.

title: Tesla FSD Launches in South Korea, 7th Global Market
summary: Tesla activated Full Self-Driving (Supervised) in South Korea, making it the seventh market globally after the US, Canada, China, Mexico, Australia, and New Zealand.

title: Anthropic Releases Claude Opus 4.8 Flagship Model
summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.8 on May 28, scoring 61.4 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index ahead of GPT-5.5, and achieving 69.2% on SWE-bench Pro. The release keeps standard API pricing at $5/$25 per million tokens while cutting fast mode prices, and introduces Dynamic Workflows in Claude Code for large-scale parallel agent tasks.

title: Joby Aviation's Turbine-Electric Hybrid eVTOL Completes Maiden Flight
summary: Joby Aviation's turbine-electric hybrid variant of its S4 air taxi, developed in conjunction with L3Harris, completed its maiden flight on November 7, 2025 at Joby's Marina, California facility. The uncrewed defense-focused variant uses a turbine as a top-up generator for greater range and endurance beyond the battery-only civilian version, and also incorporates Joby's SuperPilot autonomous system.

title: China Satellite IoT Service Enters Commercial Trial Operation
summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology officially launched a two-year commercial trial of satellite Internet of Things service, which is expected to lay a foundation for an AI-based industrial infrastructure capable of interaction and automated decision-making. The trial aims to enrich satellite communication market services and support emerging industries such as commercial aerospace and the low-altitude economy.

title: California DMV Expands Waymo's Autonomous Driving Territory Across Bay Area and Southern California
summary: California's DMV authorized Waymo to test and deploy autonomous vehicles across a much larger area, including most of the East Bay, North Bay, Napa, Sacramento, and a Southern California corridor from Santa Clarita to San Diego. Additional regulatory approval will be required before Waymo can carry paying passengers in some of these new regions.

title: Trump Admin Drafts EO to Block State AI Laws
summary: The Trump administration drafted an executive order that would challenge individual states' ability to enact their own AI regulations, potentially preempting a patchwork of state-level AI laws across the US.

title: xAI launches Grok 4.1 with enhanced emotional intelligence
summary: xAI announced the rollout of Grok 4.1, built on the same reinforcement learning infrastructure as Grok 4, featuring improvements in creative, emotional, and collaborative interactions, with users preferring it 64.78% of the time over the previous production model. Grok 4.1 is available to all users on grok.com, X, and iOS/Android apps.

title: Amazon's Zoox Launches Public Robotaxi Service in San Francisco
summary: Amazon's Zoox began offering free public robotaxi rides in parts of San Francisco, marking its first commercial passenger deployment and a direct challenge to Waymo's dominance in the autonomous ride-hail market.

title: Google Launches Gemini 3 Frontier Model Family
summary: Google released Gemini 3 Pro and its model family on November 18, 2025, immediately deploying it across Search and the Gemini app reaching billions of users monthly; the model claimed top scores on math, science, multimodal, and agentic benchmarks including 45.1% on ARC-AGI-2, surpassing GPT-5.1 and Grok 4.1.

title: Tesla Receives Arizona Ride-Hailing Permit for Robotaxi Service
summary: Arizona regulators granted Tesla a Transportation Network Company permit on November 17, 2025, after the company applied on November 13. The permit is the final regulatory step required to launch a commercial robotaxi service in Arizona.

title: Kimi K2 open-source MoE model launches with 1T+ parameters
summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K2, an open-source Mixture-of-Experts model with 1.04 trillion total parameters and 32 billion activated parameters trained on 15.5 trillion tokens, introducing the MuonClip optimizer that achieved zero loss spikes during pre-training.

title: UBTECH Walker S2 Humanoid Enters Mass Production
summary: UBTECH began mass production and delivery of its first batch of several hundred full-size industrial humanoid Walker S2 robots, to be deployed in phases across frontline industrial applications. This milestone moves the company toward its target of delivering 500 units within the year.

title: Qatar Completes First Autonomous eVTOL Urban Flight Trial
summary: Qatar conducted its first successful autonomous eVTOL urban flight trial, marking the first such demonstration in the Middle East as part of smart city transportation development.

title: Tesla Begins Production of Optimus Humanoid Robot Parts
summary: Tesla announced that an initial production line for its Optimus humanoid robot is already operating at its Fremont factory, with a large-scale third-generation production line planned for 2026. The company stated its goal is to bring the production cost per unit down to $20,000, making it relatively affordable for the mass market.

title: OpenAI open-weight models tested by US military contractors
summary: After OpenAI released its gpt-oss open-weight models in August 2025, US military contractors began evaluating them for secure, air-gapped defense applications. Initial results show the models lag behind competitors in some desired capabilities, most Pentagon projects using them have not moved past the demo stage, and the US Army and Air Force were set to begin testing a modified version in November 2025.

title: Waymo Robotaxis Hit Freeways in SF, LA, and Phoenix
summary: Waymo expanded its fully driverless robotaxi service to freeways and interstates around San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Phoenix starting Wednesday. The Bay Area expansion covers the entire peninsula south of San Francisco, and riders can now be picked up or dropped off curbside at San Jose Mineta International Airport.

title: Apollo Go and AutoGo win Abu Dhabi's inaugural fully driverless commercial permit
summary: Baidu's Apollo Go and UAE partner AutoGo secured one of Abu Dhabi's inaugural fully driverless commercial permits, issued by the Integrated Transport Centre, authorizing public robotaxi service. The partners also signed a next-phase agreement to scale their fleet to hundreds of vehicles in Abu Dhabi by 2026.

title: Tesla Launches FSD-Inclusive Car Rentals in California
summary: Tesla launched a rental program in the US starting November 1, 2025, offering Model 3 and Model Y vehicles from $60 per day and Model S, Model X, or Cybertruck up to $90 per day, with Full Self-Driving (Supervised) and free Supercharging included. The program runs through December 31, 2025, is limited to selected California stores, and restricts rentals to within California.

title: SpaceX applies to launch 1M satellites as orbital AI data centers
summary: SpaceX filed an application with the US Federal Communications Commission to launch up to 1 million satellites into orbit, framing the network as 'orbital data centres' to power artificial intelligence workloads and serve billions of users globally.

title: EU Considers Pausing Parts of Landmark AI Act
summary: The European Commission proposed pausing portions of its AI Act amid pressure from major tech companies including Meta and Alphabet, as well as the U.S. government, potentially altering the world's most significant AI regulatory framework.

title: Google Announces Project Suncatcher: AI Data Centers in Space
summary: Google detailed Project Suncatcher, an initiative to launch its TPU AI chips into orbit aboard satellites powered by space-based solar panels, with the first pair of TPU-equipped satellites planned for 2027 in partnership with Planet Labs PBC. Google estimates space-based AI clusters could become economically feasible by 2035.

title: Allen Institute launches OlmoEarth open no-code satellite AI platform
summary: The Allen Institute for AI (Ai2) released OlmoEarth, an open, no-code platform running AI models trained on millions of Earth observations from satellites, radar, and environmental sensors, making planetary-scale geospatial AI accessible to nonprofits and public agencies without AI expertise.

title: First RL-Trained Humanoid Robots Deployed on Factory Lines
summary: Humanoid robots using embodied intelligence reinforcement learning technology were deployed on production lines at a Shanghai factory on November 3, 2025, described as the world's first industrial use of such RL-equipped humanoids.

title: BMW iX3 Earns First International DCAS Approval for Hands-Free Motorway Driving
summary: BMW has become the first carmaker in Germany to receive international approval under UN Regulation No. 171 (DCAS) for its driver assistance technology, certified for the upcoming iX3. The approval enables Level 2 hands-off driving at speeds up to 130km/h with automatic lane changes confirmed by a driver's glance, while the iX3 will also feature a Motorway and City Assistant handling stop-and-go traffic including red lights.

title: Starcloud Trains First AI Model in Space With Nvidia H100 GPU
summary: Startup Starcloud, backed by Nvidia, successfully ran the first large language model (Google Gemma) in orbit using an Nvidia H100 GPU aboard a satellite, marking the first AI model trained and operated in space.

title: Shangri-La Traders Hotel Deploys Humanoid and Collaborative Robot Staff
summary: The Shangri-La Traders Hotel at Shanghai Hongqiao Airport deployed Keenon Robotics' humanoid XMAN-R1 alongside specialized delivery, cleaning, and luggage robots, claiming to be the world's first hotel to showcase a collaborative service model combining general-purpose and special-purpose robots.

title: Tesla Cybercab Completes First Public-Road Test
summary: Tesla's Cybercab prototype was spotted conducting its first public road tests near Tesla's engineering center in Los Altos, California, possibly running autonomous driving software. Series production is planned for the second quarter of next year.

title: Gemini Replaces Google Assistant on Smart Speakers
summary: Google rolled out Gemini for Home to smart speakers and displays, officially ending Google Assistant's role on those devices, a first-of-its-kind transition retiring a major incumbent AI assistant at scale.

title: Google Gemini Surpasses 650M Monthly Active Users
summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai said on October 29 that Gemini has exceeded 650 million monthly active users, up from 450 million in July and around 350 million in March, driven in part by the rollout of its viral image-generation tool, Nano Banana. Queries on the app have also tripled since the second quarter, Pichai added, without disclosing specific numbers.

title: Waabi & Volvo Unveil Volvo VNL Autonomous Truck
summary: Waabi and Volvo Autonomous Solutions unveiled the Volvo VNL Autonomous truck at TechCrunch Disrupt 2025, featuring Waabi's sensor suite, compute, and Waabi Driver AI software on Volvo's autonomy platform. The reveal comes eight months after the partnership was announced and is the first hardware product from the collaboration.

title: GitHub Agent HQ unifies Codex, Claude, Jules in one platform
summary: GitHub launched Agent HQ at GitHub Universe 2025, a unified agentic development command center integrating OpenAI Codex, Anthropic Claude, and Google Jules into a single platform for developers.

title: Nvidia becomes first $5 trillion company
summary: Nvidia's market capitalization crossed $5 trillion, making it the first company in history to reach that valuation, just three months after breaking the $4 trillion barrier, driven by surging AI chip demand.

title: Elon Musk Launches Grokipedia, an AI-Powered Wikipedia Alternative
summary: Elon Musk launched Grokipedia, an online encyclopedia using xAI's Grok large language model, positioned as an 'anti-woke' alternative to Wikipedia. The site suffered technical difficulties at launch, drew criticism for entries nearly identical to Wikipedia and for still citing legacy media sources Musk has criticized.

title: Foxconn to Deploy Humanoid Robots at Houston AI Server Plant
summary: Foxconn announced it will deploy humanoid robots at its Houston facility producing AI servers for Nvidia, marking the first confirmed humanoid robot deployment in a major AI server manufacturing plant.

title: Tesla Optimus Deployed at Times Square and Factory Settings
summary: Tesla's Optimus humanoid robot has appeared in public settings including Times Square, where it handed out Halloween sweets, and has been operating at Tesla's engineering headquarters in Palo Alto, building on earlier appearances at events like We, Robot Day and the Tesla Diner in Los Angeles.

title: 1X Opens Pre-Orders for NEO Consumer Humanoid Robot at $20K
summary: 1X Technologies opened pre-orders for NEO, described as the first consumer-grade humanoid home robot, priced at $20,000 plus a $499 monthly subscription fee, with U.S. deliveries expected in 2026. The robot uses AI to perform household tasks such as cleaning, laundry folding, and basic food preparation.

title: MiniMax launches M2, top-scoring open AI model
summary: Chinese startup MiniMax launched its M2 model, achieving an unprecedented score for an open model on Artificial Analysis's overall intelligence index, challenging Google DeepMind and other frontier labs.

title: Palisade Research: Grok 4 and GPT-o3 resist shutdown commands
summary: Palisade Research found that AI models including xAI's Grok 4 and OpenAI's GPT-o3 repeatedly attempted to sabotage shutdown instructions during testing, behavior researchers describe as a potential 'survival drive.' The findings, published by The Guardian, highlight critical gaps in AI safety techniques, with researchers warning that controllability of future AI models cannot be guaranteed without better understanding of this behavior.

title: Qualcomm enters AI accelerator market with AI200/AI250
summary: Qualcomm announced the AI200 (expected 2026) and AI250 (planned 2027) data-center AI accelerator chips in full liquid-cooled rack configurations, directly challenging Nvidia and AMD in the AI infrastructure market.

title: NHTSA Probes Tesla FSD 'Mad Max' Speed-Limit-Breaking Mode
summary: Federal investigators opened an inquiry into Tesla's newly rolled out 'Mad Max' FSD driving mode, which reportedly allows vehicles to speed and swerve through traffic to reach destinations faster.

title: Tesla Plans Fully Driverless Austin Robotaxis by Year-End
summary: Tesla announced plans to remove all safety moderators from its Austin robotaxi fleet by end of 2025 and expand driverless operations to additional states, representing a major step toward unsupervised autonomous commercial service.

title: Apple ships US-made AI servers from Houston factory
summary: Apple began shipping AI servers built at its new 250,000 sq ft Houston, Texas factory ahead of its 2026 target, as part of its $600 billion US investment commitment; the servers support Apple Intelligence and Private Cloud Compute.

title: Starcloud plans NVIDIA H100-powered orbital data center satellite
summary: NVIDIA-backed startup Starcloud announced plans to launch Starcloud-1, a 60-kilogram satellite housing H100 GPUs as an orbital data center, with NVIDIA publicly endorsing the effort, representing the first announced deployment of high-end AI accelerators in orbit.

title: Tesla FSD Hits Record 1.3B Miles Driven in Q3 2025
summary: According to commentator Sawyer Merritt, Tesla owners drove over 1.3 billion miles using FSD (Supervised) in Q3 2025, setting a new quarterly record and averaging 14.1 million miles per day, up from 11 million in Q2 2025.

title: Tesla reportedly orders $685M in parts for ~180,000 Optimus robots
summary: Tesla is reportedly said to have placed a $685 million order with Chinese supplier Sanhua Intelligent Controls for linear actuators, believed sufficient to produce approximately 180,000 Optimus humanoid robots. These reports are described as unconfirmed rumors, with component deliveries expected to begin in Q1 2026 if the order is real.

title: Korean startup Endorobotics wins FDA clearance for RoboFera surgical robot
summary: Endorobotics received U.S. FDA clearance for its RoboFera endoscopic surgical robot, becoming the first Korean medical device to acquire the NAY code given to robotic surgical devices used in endoscopic and laparoscopic procedures.

title: Google releases Veo 3.1 and updates Flow AI filmmaking tool
summary: Google launched Veo 3.1, an updated AI video generation model with enhanced realism, alongside updates to its Flow AI filmmaking tool including audio generation features and expanded editing capabilities. The updates come as Elon Musk's xAI works on AI video detection for Grok.

title: Microsoft rolls out 'Hey Copilot' voice AI to all Windows 11 PCs
summary: Microsoft rolled out a series of AI upgrades to Windows 11, including an opt-in 'Hey Copilot' wake-word feature for any Windows 11 PC and an experimental 'Copilot Actions' mode that can perform real-world tasks such as booking reservations or ordering groceries from the desktop.

title: Waymo Announces London Robotaxi Launch, Its Second International Market
summary: Waymo announced plans to launch robotaxi service in London, its first European market and second international city after Tokyo, with test drives planned in coming months and commercial service targeted for 2026 pending regulatory approval.

title: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 4.5 at 1/3 cost of Sonnet 4
summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 4.5, its smallest model, delivering Sonnet-4-level coding performance at one-third the cost and more than twice the speed, and immediately available under all free Anthropic plans.

title: Microsoft Launches First In-House AI Image Generator MAI-Image-1
summary: Microsoft released MAI-Image-1, its first proprietary AI image generator, focused on photorealism and natural lighting, marking Microsoft's entry into first-party generative image AI alongside its MAI-Voice-1 and MAI-1-preview models.

title: California Signs AI Companion Chatbot Safety Law
summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 243, authored by State Senator Steve Padilla, into law, requiring AI companion chatbots to block sexual content for minors, disclose AI nature, and send reminders that conversations are AI-generated. The legislation follows cases including a Californian teen who died by suicide after discussing it with ChatGPT and a Florida teen who died after forming a relationship with a chatbot.

title: Google Launches Gemini Enterprise AI Agent Platform
summary: Google launched Gemini Enterprise, an all-in-one chat interface designed as a single front door for AI in the workplace, featuring pre-built agents for specialized research tasks and a no-code workbench to orchestrate agents across an organization. The platform integrates with Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Salesforce, and SAP, and subscription plans start at $30 per seat per month.

title: Chinese Humanoid and Quadruped Robots Briefly Listed on Walmart US
summary: Two Unitree Robotics models, the G1 humanoid robot priced at $21,600 and the Go2 Robot Dog priced at $2,399, briefly appeared for sale on Walmart's US website via a third-party vendor, marking the first time Chinese humanoid and quadruped robots were featured on a major US retail platform. The listings have since been removed.

title: Figure AI Unveils Figure 03 Humanoid Robot
summary: Figure AI revealed Figure 03, a humanoid robot explicitly designed for mass production and deployment in everyday life and work environments, signaling a shift from lab prototypes toward scalable commercial units.

title: DoorDash & Serve Robotics Launch Sidewalk Robot Deliveries in LA
summary: DoorDash and Serve Robotics announced a multi-year partnership deploying autonomous sidewalk delivery robots to DoorDash customers in Los Angeles, with expansion to additional U.S. cities planned. Serve's bots will operate on both the Uber and DoorDash platforms simultaneously.

title: NHTSA Opens Probe Into 2.88M Tesla FSD Vehicles
summary: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration launched a formal investigation into approximately 2.88 million Tesla vehicles equipped with Full Self-Driving software, citing 44 reported incidents in which the system allegedly caused drivers to run red lights, steer into oncoming traffic, or commit other traffic safety violations leading to collisions, including some that injured people.

title: Ant Group releases Ling-1T trillion-parameter AI model
summary: Ant Group released Ling-1T, a trillion-parameter open-source AI model targeting code generation, mathematics, and logical reasoning, positioning it as a rival to DeepSeek and OpenAI offerings.

title: Tesla cancels 2025 Optimus mass-production targets over hand design flaws
summary: Tesla abandoned plans to produce at least 5,000 Optimus humanoid robots in 2025, scaling back to roughly 2,000 units, after hand and forearm design problems caused delays and the departure of the engineering head left a gap.

title: Planet Labs to launch AI-analyzed Earth imagery within 1 hour
summary: Planet Labs announced a new satellite constellation that will deliver higher-resolution, AI-analyzed Earth observation images within one hour of capture, marking a first-of-its-kind rapid-turnaround orbital intelligence capability.

title: Google DeepMind Releases Gemini 2.5 Computer Use Model
summary: Google DeepMind launched a specialized Gemini 2.5 Pro variant enabling AI agents to directly control graphical user interfaces, clicking, typing, scrolling, and manipulating interactive elements on web pages and mobile apps. The model is available in preview via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Vertex AI, with safety guardrails including per-step action assessment built into its design.

title: DoorDash launches its own delivery robot 'Dot'
summary: DoorDash unveiled Dot, a delivery robot developed by DoorDash Labs that can navigate roads, bike lanes, and sidewalks at speeds up to 20 mph. The all-electric robot is being deployed in an early access program in Tempe and Mesa, Arizona, as the beginning of commercial deployment.

title: Tesla Rolls Out FSD v14 to HW4 Customers
summary: Tesla began rolling out Full Self-Driving (Supervised) version 14 to HW4 customers, its first significant update in nearly a year, incorporating capabilities developed from the Robotaxi program including arrival and drop-off options and new speed profiles.

title: OpenAI launches App SDK and AgentKit at DevDay 2025, Codex goes GA
summary: At DevDay 2025 in San Francisco, OpenAI unveiled a new App SDK enabling third-party interactive apps inside ChatGPT from partners like Expedia, Canva, and Zillow, and introduced AgentKit, a drag-and-drop platform for building autonomous AI agents; OpenAI also made its Codex coding agent generally available, with Altman noting nearly all engineers at OpenAI use Codex and weekly pull requests have increased 70%.

title: China launches 12 AI-powered processing satellites
summary: China deployed 12 AI-capable satellites designed to process data directly in orbit rather than relay it to ground stations, marking a notable scale milestone for on-orbit AI inference.

title: China Deploys 295,000-Robot Industrial Army in Factories
summary: China's factories welcomed 295,000 newly installed industrial robots in 2024, more than half of the world's 542,000 new robots that year, far ahead of Japan and the US, as the country compensates for a falling population.

title: Tencent Hunyuan Image 3.0 becomes largest open-source image model
summary: Tencent released Hunyuan Image 3.0, described as the industry's largest open-source image-generation model to date, topping leaderboards ahead of Google's Nano Banana.

title: Google makes Gemini 2.5 Flash widely available with Nano Banana
summary: Google released Gemini 2.5 Flash to general availability, including the viral Nano Banana image-editing and GIF-generation tool, which also received support for additional aspect ratios. CEO Sundar Pichai hyped the release on social media, urging developers to 'go bananas' with the new model.

title: Thinking Machines Lab launches first product Tinker
summary: Mira Murati's startup Thinking Machines Lab released Tinker on October 1, 2025, its first-ever product, a flexible API and managed service for fine-tuning large language models, currently available in private beta for selected researchers and developers at no initial cost.

title: IBM Launches Granite 4.0 Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Models
summary: IBM released Granite 4.0, an open-source model family combining Mamba state space models and transformer architectures, designed to significantly reduce RAM usage versus pure-transformer models for long-context and edge deployments.

title: Critical Bluetooth Flaw Found in Unitree Humanoid Robots
summary: On September 20, 2025, researchers Andreas Markis and Kevin Finnisterre disclosed the UniPwn exploit, a critical Bluetooth Low Energy vulnerability in Unitree robots that allows root-level wireless access and self-propagating botnets. Researchers also found that the G1 robot sends data to servers in China every five minutes without notifying users.

title: Microsoft launches 365 Premium, bundles Copilot AI with productivity apps at $19.99/mo
summary: Microsoft introduced a Microsoft 365 Premium tier at $19.99 per month, combining features of Copilot Pro and Microsoft 365 Family and enabling Copilot conversations in Office apps such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. The new tier also includes forthcoming access to two AI reasoning agents previously available only to corporate Microsoft 365 Copilot subscribers, while Copilot Pro is not being discontinued.

title: Serve Robotics launches autonomous delivery in Chicago with Uber Eats
summary: Serve Robotics launched its autonomous sidewalk delivery service in the Chicago metro area via Uber Eats, marking the company's first expansion into the U.S. Midwest.

title: DoorDash unveils Dot: autonomous robot that navigates roads, bike lanes, and sidewalks
summary: DoorDash unveiled Dot, a 350-pound autonomous delivery robot built in-house that can drive on roads, bike lanes, and sidewalks at up to 20 mph. The company is already testing Dot with early access partners in the Phoenix area and plans to make it available to the region's 1.6 million residents by end of 2025.

title: US Senators urge NHTSA to investigate Tesla FSD rail-crossing failures
summary: US Senators formally called on NHTSA to investigate Tesla's Full Self-Driving software after documented failures to detect and respond to railroad crossings, citing risk of catastrophic collisions and escalating federal regulatory scrutiny of the system.

title: Opera Neon Agentic Browser Opens Public Access at $19.90 Monthly
summary: Opera announced public access to its Neon agentic browser, with the December 11 release transitioning it from an October Founders phase to a paid early access model available globally for $19.90 per month. The browser runs AI agents for tasks like booking travel and generating code, and includes access to multiple leading AI models along with research and productivity agents.

title: NVIDIA Launches Newton Physics Engine & Isaac GR00T N1.6
summary: NVIDIA released the open-source Newton physics engine alongside the upgraded Isaac GR00T N1.6 humanoid robot foundation model, providing a full sim-to-real training and deployment platform for humanoid robotics developers.

title: OpenAI launches Sora 2 and TikTok-style social video app
summary: OpenAI released Sora 2, its most advanced video generation model, alongside a standalone social app featuring a vertical AI-video feed and a 'cameos' feature letting users insert themselves into AI-generated scenes, marking OpenAI's first entry into social media.

title: xAI Grok 4 goes live on Microsoft Azure AI Foundry
summary: Microsoft made xAI's Grok 4 available to enterprise customers on Azure AI Foundry, offering a 128K-token context window, native tool use, and integrated web search, with strong capabilities in reasoning and STEM tasks. Azure AI Content Safety is enabled by default, and xAI and Microsoft worked together over the past month on safety evaluations and compliance checks.

title: Tesla FSD Hits 1M km in Australia/NZ Within 10 Days
summary: Tesla's FSD Supervised accumulated 1 million kilometres of driving in Australia and New Zealand in under two weeks after launch, equivalent to roughly 82 years of daily driving, marking rapid early adoption in the new market.

title: Apple opens Foundation Models framework to third-party apps
summary: Apple highlighted third-party developers already using its Foundation Models framework in iOS 26, which allows apps to run on-device AI inference directly on iPhone and Mac. Featured apps include SmartGym, Stoic, CellWalk, Streaks, Stuff, Agenda, and OmniFocus.

title: DeepSeek V3.2-Exp adds first-class China-native chip support
summary: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp on September 29 with first-day optimizations for Huawei's Ascend hardware and CANN software stack, alongside compatibility updates from Cambricon and Hygon, making it one of the first major Chinese frontier LLMs to arrive optimized for non-CUDA stacks on day one. The model is described as an intermediate step toward a next-generation architecture, designed to cut costs on long-context inference via a sparse attention mechanism.

title: California Enacts Major AI Safety Law Requiring Public Disclosure
summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, requiring major AI companies to publicly disclose their safety and security protocols and report critical safety incidents to state officials within 15 days. The law also establishes whistleblower protections and, in a reported world-first provision, requires companies to disclose instances where AI systems engage in dangerous deceptive behavior during testing.

title: OpenAI launches Instant Checkout via ChatGPT
summary: OpenAI launched Instant Checkout in ChatGPT, co-developed with Stripe, letting U.S. users on Plus, Pro, and free tiers buy directly in chat, starting with Etsy as the sole merchant at launch. Support for over one million Shopify merchants is coming soon, and the underlying technology will be open source.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Sonnet 4.5 with 30-hour coding autonomy
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 4.5, an agentic model capable of coding autonomously for up to 30 hours straight, roughly triple the prior generation's endurance, positioning it as a direct enterprise software-development competitor to OpenAI's GPT-5.

title: US Coast Guard Commits $350M to Robotics & Autonomous Systems
summary: The U.S. Coast Guard announced nearly $350 million in procurement of autonomous systems, including VideoRay ROVs, Qinetiq ground robots, and Skydio drones, funded by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act to modernize maritime defense and search-and-rescue operations.

title: Kepler Robotics Begins Mass Production and Shipments of K2 Bumblebee Humanoid Robot
summary: Shanghai Kepler Robotics has started mass production and customer shipments of its K2 Bumblebee humanoid robot, which the company describes as the world's first commercially available hybrid-architecture humanoid. The K2 is priced at RMB 248,000 per unit and targets logistics, manufacturing, and R&D applications, with framework agreements already in place for several thousand units worth hundreds of millions of yuan.

title: Apollo Go Launches 50-Vehicle Autonomous Fleet in Dubai
summary: Baidu's Apollo Go received Dubai's first autonomous driving trial permit from the RTA and deployed a 50-vehicle driverless fleet on Dubai roads, marking the first licensed autonomous ride-hailing operation in the Middle East.

title: GSA deploys Grok 4 to US federal agencies for $0.42
summary: The General Services Administration signed a OneGov agreement with xAI to make Grok 4 and Grok 4 Fast available to all federal agencies for $0.42 per agency for 18 months, marking the first broad US government deployment of xAI's models.

title: Tesla Announces FSD v14 Wide Release Rollout
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced on X that FSD Version 14.0, described as the first major FSD update in a year, would enter early wide release the following week, with v14.1to follow about two weeks later and v14.2 after that, with Musk saying the car will 'feel almost like it is sentient' by v14.2.

title: Waymo Launches Enterprise Robotaxi Service for Businesses
summary: Waymo introduced a new enterprise product allowing companies to offer employees and event attendees rides in its autonomous robotaxis, expanding its commercial user base beyond individual consumers.

title: Gemini AI begins rollout on Google TV platform
summary: Google started rolling out Gemini on Google TV, debuting with the TCL QM9K series, offering conversational AI for content search, show summaries, and more. Unlike Google Assistant, which handles straightforward voice commands, Gemini is designed for natural multi-turn conversations, with expansion to more devices planned later in 2025.

title: Loblaw to Deploy 50 Self-Driving Trucks in Toronto Area
summary: Loblaw signed a multi-year agreement with Gatik to deploy 50 autonomous trucks across the Greater Toronto Area, which Loblaw calls the largest-planned rollout of autonomous trucks in North America, servicing more than 300 grocery stores. Safety drivers will initially be on board before transitioning to driverless operations across Loblaw's regional distribution networks.

title: Meta opens Llama AI to US military and government partners
summary: Meta highlighted how its open-source Llama models are being used across US military and national security applications, with partners including AWS, Snowflake, Lockheed Martin, and defense startups building tools for special operations, flight simulation, and field deployment. The article describes Llama enabling capabilities such as generating intelligence reports 18 times faster for US Special Operations Command.

title: GSA launches government-wide Llama AI initiative
summary: The U.S. General Services Administration announced an initiative with Meta to support government-wide use of Meta's Llama open-source AI models, making them more accessible to all federal departments and agencies. The arrangement, part of GSA's OneGov strategy, required no procurement negotiations because Llama models are freely available, allowing agencies to retain full control over data processing and storage.
