title: Grab & WeRide Announce Singapore Robotaxi Service
summary: Grab and China's WeRide announced a partnership to launch the Ai.R autonomous shuttle service in Singapore's Punggol residential area under an agreement with the Land Transport Authority, with passenger service set to begin by early 2026. The fleet will consist of 11 WeRide vehicles across two routes, and the vehicles will be the first to attain Singapore's Milestone 1 certification for use in Punggol.

title: UniPwn exploit enables root takeover of Unitree robots
summary: Researchers disclosed the 'UniPwn' vulnerability on September 20, 2025, showing that a Bluetooth Low Energy flaw in Unitree's Go2, B2, G1, and H1 robots allows attackers to gain root-level control wirelessly; the flaw is described as 'wormable,' enabling potential botnet-scale compromise of deployed commercial robots.

title: xAI launches Grok 4 Fast, a cost-efficient reasoning model
summary: xAI released Grok 4 Fast, a reasoning model that reduces average thinking tokens by 40% compared to Grok 4, yielding an estimated 98% decrease in cost for equivalent benchmark performance. It supports a 2-million token context window, both reasoning and non-reasoning modes, and tool-use capabilities including web browsing and X search.

title: NHTSA Issues Performance-Based AV Regulatory Framework
summary: The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration announced a new performance-based framework for autonomous vehicles on September 20, 2025, shifting federal oversight from prescriptive hardware requirements to real-world outcome metrics, a foundational regulatory change for AV deployment at scale.

title: Apple Watch Series 11 gains AI blood pressure detection
summary: Apple Watch Series 11 launched with an FDA-cleared AI-powered high blood pressure notification feature derived from existing sensor data rather than a dedicated blood pressure monitor, a first for the platform.

title: Google adds Gemini AI assistant to Chrome for U.S. users
summary: Google announced it is rolling out Gemini in Chrome to Mac and Windows users in the U.S. and to mobile devices, making the assistant more widely available after previously restricting it to certain subscription holders. The integration lets users get help with webpage content, work across tabs, and access Google apps like Calendar, YouTube, and Maps without leaving the browser.

title: DeepSeek R1 training cost confirmed at $294K in Nature
summary: DeepSeek published a peer-reviewed paper in Nature disclosing that its R1 reasoning model cost just $294,000 to train, the first official cost figure released by the company, far below comparable U.S. frontier model training costs.

title: Tesla signs Optimus letter of intent with PharmAGRI: up to 10,000 robots
summary: PharmAGRI signed a letter of intent with Tesla to deploy up to 10,000 Optimus humanoid robots from the third generation onward across farm operations, pharmaceutical ingredient synthesis, and drug manufacturing facilities.

title: BlackSky wins NGA contract for AI-powered satellite change detection
summary: BlackSky Technology received a delivery order from the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency to deploy its proprietary AI for automated change detection across millions of square kilometers, covering natural resources, infrastructure, and military activity.

title: Tesla FSD Supervised Launches in Australia & New Zealand
summary: Tesla activated Full Self-Driving (Supervised) for eligible Model 3 and Model Y owners with Hardware 4 cameras in Australia and New Zealand on September 17, making them the first right-hand drive markets where the technology is publicly available. Customers who have purchased FSD Capability can apply the update, while a subscription option at $149 per month is also coming soon.

title: Figure & Brookfield partner to build world's largest humanoid training dataset
summary: Robotics firm Figure announced a strategic partnership with $1 trillion asset manager Brookfield to create the world's largest humanoid AI pretraining dataset across 100,000 residential units, with Brookfield also investing in Figure's Series C and committing to scale robot deployment across its commercial properties.

title: Italy Becomes First EU Nation to Enact Comprehensive AI Law
summary: Italy's parliament approved a national AI law covering privacy, oversight, and child access, making Italy the first EU member state with comprehensive AI legislation aligned with the EU AI Act.

title: Armada & Sophia Space Launch Earth-to-Orbit Edge AI Platform
summary: Armada and Sophia Space debuted a unified Earth-to-orbit edge AI platform connecting ground-based data centers with orbital compute nodes for real-time satellite analytics, representing a first-of-its-kind commercial hybrid ground-space AI infrastructure.

title: California SB 243 AI Companion Chatbot Bill Passes Legislature
summary: California's SB 243 passed the legislature and is awaiting the governor's signature; if enacted, it would be the first U.S. state law requiring AI companion operators to implement safety protocols and imposing legal liability for failures.

title: Zoox Opens First Public Robotaxi Rides in Las Vegas
summary: Amazon's Zoox began offering rides to the general public in Las Vegas, marking the first US deployment of a purpose-built robotaxi with no driver controls or steering wheel.

title: Tesla Robotaxi Expands to 171 Sq Miles in Austin
summary: Tesla expanded its robotaxi service area in Austin to 171 square miles, surpassing Waymo's coverage footprint in the city. Separately, the Tesla Robotaxi app exceeded 2 million downloads on its first day, outpacing historical highs for both Uber and Waymo.

title: Alibaba releases first trillion-parameter Qwen3 model
summary: Alibaba launched Qwen-3-Max-Preview, its first model exceeding 1 trillion parameters, targeting direct competition with OpenAI and Google DeepMind at the frontier scale.

title: Tesla Cancels Six-Year Dojo Supercomputer Project
summary: Tesla disbanded its Dojo supercomputer team and terminated the project in August 2025, after six years of development. Elon Musk cited Dojo 2 as an evolutionary dead-end, saying all paths lead to the AI6 chip, and Tesla has shifted toward partner-supplied hardware including NVIDIA GPUs and AI6 chips ordered from Samsung.

title: Boston Dynamics and TRI demonstrate Atlas using single AI model for loco-manipulation
summary: Boston Dynamics and the Toyota Research Institute demonstrated that their Atlas humanoid robot can use a single unified large behavior model to control both walking and grasping, replacing the usual approach of separate models for each. The model also shows emergent skills, such as recovering from a dropped item without being explicitly trained to do so.

title: Switzerland launches Apertus open-source national LLM
summary: Switzerland launched Apertus, an open-source large language model trained on data from public sources that allowed scraping, with weights, training data, source code, and development process available on HuggingFace as an alternative to proprietary models like ChatGPT or Claude.

title: Google announces Gemini integration on Home devices starting October 1
summary: Google posted on X that Gemini will be available on Google Home devices from October 1, 2025, replacing Google Assistant on those devices. The announcement also included a link for users to sign up for updates, though details about paid versus free features remain unclear.

title: Planet Labs Releases Pelican-3 First Light Images, More Launches Planned
summary: Planet Labs released first light images from its Pelican-3 satellite, captured on September 5, 2025, over Turin, Italy. Pelican-3 and Pelican-4 join the growing constellation offering up to 40cm-class multispectral imagery across 6 bands and NVIDIA Jetson AI chips for on-orbit edge computing, with a next generation targeting 30cm imagery expected to begin launching the following year.

title: Tesla Master Plan Part IV Pivots Company to Optimus Robots
summary: Tesla published Master Plan Part IV, formally repositioning the company around Optimus humanoid robots and AI autonomy; Musk projected robotics will represent ~80% of Tesla's total value, de-emphasizing its core EV business.

title: Axiom Space & Red Hat Deploy AxDCU-1 Data Center to ISS
summary: Axiom Space and Red Hat launched the AxDCU-1 prototype data center to the International Space Station on August 24, 2025, aboard SpaceX's 33rd commercial resupply mission, marking the first test of terrestrial-grade edge computing hardware in orbit. The deployment, sponsored by the ISS National Laboratory, aims to validate autonomous computing infrastructure in space and reduce reliance on costly satellite downlinks by enabling real-time on-board data processing.

title: Microsoft launches first in-house AI models MAI-Voice-1 and MAI-1-preview
summary: Microsoft announced MAI-Voice-1, a natural speech generation model already used in Copilot Daily and Copilot Podcasts, and MAI-1-preview, a mixture-of-experts text model being tested on LMArena and rolled out for certain Copilot text use cases. The launch marks the first models developed and trained entirely in-house by Microsoft AI under Mustafa Suleyman, though Microsoft stated it will continue using OpenAI models alongside its own.

title: Meta explores integrating Google Gemini and OpenAI models into Meta AI
summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs leaders have explored integrating Google's Gemini and OpenAI models to power Meta AI and other AI features in Meta's social media apps, according to The Information. Any such deals are described as likely temporary steps to enhance Meta's AI products until its own models advance, with a priority on ensuring Llama 5 can compete with rivals.

title: Tesla FSD testing begins in Boring Co. Las Vegas tunnels
summary: The Boring Company began testing Tesla Full Self-Driving in its Las Vegas Convention Center Loop tunnels, marking the first deployment of FSD in the underground transit system.

title: OpenAI Codex Agent Gets GPT-5, VS Code Extension & GitHub Reviews
summary: OpenAI released a major update to its Codex AI coding agent, rebuilding the CLI with GPT-5 agentic capabilities, adding a new IDE extension for VS Code and Cursor, and enabling automated GitHub pull request reviews via comment tagging. The update creates a unified agent across a developer's IDE, terminal, and cloud environments, available to all paying ChatGPT subscribers including Plus, Pro, Team, Edu, and Enterprise plans.

title: Planet Labs Launches AI-Enabled Pelican-3 & Pelican-4 Satellites
summary: Planet Labs announced the successful launch of two high-resolution, AI-enabled satellites, Pelican-3 and Pelican-4, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base. The satellites feature on-orbit computing capability through a partnership with NVIDIA, which equips them with Jetson AI platforms.

title: Saudi Arabia launches Humain Chat Arabic AI app
summary: Saudi Arabia's PIF-owned Humain launched Humain Chat, an Arabic-language AI app powered by the ALLAM 34B model, marking the first sovereign Arabic large-language-model consumer deployment in the Kingdom.

title: EHang Delivers 68 Autonomous eVTOLs in Record Quarter
summary: EHang delivered 68 units of EH216 series eVTOL aircraft in Q2 2025, recording 464% quarter-over-quarter revenue growth to $20.5M and completing over 10,000 safe flights in H1 2025, marking a concrete scale milestone for autonomous air taxi operations.

title: Chinese humanoid robot firms adopt Nvidia Jetson AGX Thor
summary: Unitree Robotics, AgiBot, Galbot, Engine AI, and UBTech Robotics became early adopters of Nvidia's Jetson AGX Thor compute module for humanoid robots. Unitree's founder and CEO cited faster decision-making and higher autonomy as key gains from the new platform.

title: xAI sues Apple and OpenAI over alleged AI monopoly
summary: Elon Musk's xAI filed a 61-page antitrust lawsuit in U.S. federal court in Texas accusing Apple and OpenAI of illegally conspiring to thwart AI competition and lock up markets via their App Store agreement.

title: xAI open-sources Grok 2.5 model
summary: Elon Musk's xAI released Grok 2.5 as an open-source model available to developers, with Musk pledging to open-source Grok 3 within approximately six months.

title: Orbital Data Center Launches to ISS for Edge Computing Tests
summary: An orbital data center built with Red Hat and Axiom Space launched to the International Space Station aboard a cargo mission to test real-time edge computing and AI processing in orbit, a first-of-its-kind deployment of a commercial data center node in space.

title: Waymo Gets First-Ever AV Testing Permit in New York City
summary: Waymo received New York City's first autonomous vehicle testing permit, allowing it to deploy up to 8 Jaguar I-Pace SUVs in Manhattan and Downtown Brooklyn through late September with a safety operator present. The permit, issued under a new AV safety regime launched by Mayor Eric Adams in 2024, marks a regulatory milestone for driverless vehicle testing in the country's largest city.

title: NHTSA Opens Probe Into Tesla Over Autopilot/FSD Crash Reporting
summary: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration launched a formal investigation into Tesla after finding the company had not reported crashes involving Autopilot and Full Self-Driving within the legally required five-day window, with Tesla attributing the delays to a data collection issue it says has been fixed.

title: Google publishes first per-query AI energy data
summary: Google released the first industry disclosure of per-query AI energy and water consumption, reporting a typical Gemini text prompt uses 0.24 watt-hours of electricity (equivalent to running a microwave for about one second) and 0.26 ml of water, the most granular transparency data yet from a major AI provider.

title: Boston Dynamics & Toyota deploy Large Behavior Model on Atlas
summary: Boston Dynamics and Toyota Research Institute demonstrated a Large Behavior Model (LBM) powering the Atlas humanoid robot, enabling it to perform long, continuous sequences of complex manipulation and locomotion tasks without hand-coded instructions for each action, a first-of-its-kind integration of foundation-model-scale AI into a physical humanoid.

title: IBM & NASA release Surya solar-weather AI model
summary: IBM and NASA released Surya, an open-source foundation model trained on high-resolution solar observation data to predict solar flares and space weather events that threaten Earth and space-based technology.

title: ByteDance releases Seed-OSS-36B with 512K token context
summary: ByteDance released Seed-OSS-36B as an open-source model featuring a native 512,000-token context window, twice that of OpenAI's GPT-5 family, marking a new scale threshold for open long-context models.

title: DeepSeek V3.1 released as 685B open-source model
summary: DeepSeek released V3.1, a 685-billion parameter open-source model with hybrid reasoning and native support for Chinese domestic chips, available at zero cost on Hugging Face.

title: Serve Robotics Acquires Vayu Robotics for AI Foundation Models
summary: Serve Robotics acquired Vayu Robotics, an urban robot navigation company using large-scale AI foundation models, in a deal comprising 1.69 million shares upfront plus a 560,000-share earnout, to accelerate autonomous sidewalk delivery capabilities.

title: China deploys Wukong AI model aboard Tiangong space station
summary: China applied the Wukong AI large language model aboard its Tiangong space station for the first time, carried to orbit by the Tianzhou-9 cargo spacecraft. It assisted astronauts in preparing for extravehicular activities and provided intelligent, specialized support for in-orbit work including emergency troubleshooting and ground-space coordination.

title: World's First Humanoid Robot Games Open in Beijing
summary: China hosted the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, with more than 500 humanoid robots in 280 teams from 16 countries expected to compete in 26 sports including basketball and kickboxing. Unitree's H1 robot won the opening 1,500-metre race, with Unitree also taking third place.

title: Google launches Gemma 3 270M on-device model for low-power inference
summary: Google has released Gemma 3 270M, a 270 million parameter model designed for task-specific fine-tuning and low-power on-device inference, with internal tests showing it used only 0.75% battery for 25 conversations on a Pixel 9 Pro. The model supports a 32K token context window, over 140 languages, and is available on platforms including Hugging Face, Ollama, and Kaggle.

title: Indian Army Deploys 100 AI Robotic Mules Along LoC
summary: The Indian Army deployed 100 AI-powered Multi-Utility Legged Equipment (MULE) robots along the Line of Control in Jammu & Kashmir to support surveillance and logistics operations.

title: China's GEAIR: first AI robot for autonomous hybrid pollination
summary: Chinese scientists unveiled GEAIR, claimed to be the world's first AI-powered robot capable of performing hybrid crop pollination entirely without human hands, targeting large-scale seed production. The system autonomously identifies and pollinates flowers, reducing labor and error in agricultural breeding.

title: Google DeepMind Launches AlphaEarth Foundations AI Model
summary: Google DeepMind launched AlphaEarth Foundations, an AI model that fuses satellite imagery, radar, 3D mapping, and climate simulations into high-resolution 10-by-10-metre embeddings covering 2017 to 2024, now publicly available in Google Earth Engine. The model achieves an average 24% reduction in error rates compared with earlier AI models and is already being used by more than 50 organizations for environmental monitoring and land-use analysis.

title: Baidu Apollo Go Robotaxi Falls Into Construction Pit With Passenger
summary: A Baidu Apollo Go robotaxi fell into a deep construction pit while carrying a passenger in Chongqing, China on August 6, 2025; the female passenger was uninjured and rescued by local residents. How the vehicle bypassed the construction site's barriers and warning signs remained unclear, and the incident sparked widespread discussion on Chinese social media about robotaxi safety.

title: Tesla Kills Dojo Supercomputer Program for FSD Training
summary: Tesla shut down its Dojo supercomputer program, which had been built specifically to train its Full Self-Driving AI on video footage from the fleet, representing a major strategic reversal after years of investment in the custom AI training infrastructure.

title: Google launches Jules AI coding agent out of beta
summary: Google officially launched Jules, an asynchronous AI coding agent powered by Gemini 2.5 Pro, into general availability with GitHub integration and free and paid tiers. Jules clones codebases into Google Cloud virtual machines and can fix or update code, open branches, and submit pull requests while developers work on other tasks.

title: China Tests Armed 'Robot Wolves' in Military Drill
summary: China deployed armed quadruped 'robot wolves' alongside soldiers and drones in a PLA military exercise, marking the first public appearance of the robots in a Chinese military drill. The robots carried rifles, climbed obstacles, and maintained pace with infantry during training activities including precision strikes, reconnaissance, and coordinated breakthroughs.

title: GPT-5 goes live in Microsoft 365 Copilot
summary: Microsoft deployed OpenAI's GPT-5 across Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio, making the model available to enterprise users at scale on the same day as the announcement.

title: NHTSA Grants Zoox Exemption, Clearing Path for Amazon Robotaxis
summary: The NHTSA granted Amazon's autonomous vehicle subsidiary Zoox a federal safety exemption, allowing its purpose-built bidirectional robotaxis to operate on public roads, a key regulatory first for the vehicle design.

title: OpenAI launches GPT-5 to all ChatGPT users
summary: OpenAI released GPT-5, described as its most advanced model to date, rolling it out to all ChatGPT users including a free tier starting Thursday. OpenAI claims the model offers PhD-level expertise, fewer hallucinations, and improved reasoning capabilities.

title: Illinois Enacts AI Mental Health Regulation Law
summary: Illinois signed and enacted a law on August 1, 2025 regulating AI use in mental health contexts, with implications for AI makers, therapists, psychologists, psychiatrists, and other mental health professionals. The article notes the law is confined to Illinois but predicts similar legislation will follow in other states and potentially at the federal level.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 4.1
summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.1, the successor to Claude Opus 4, with improved coding, reasoning, and agentic task capabilities. The model advances SWE-bench Verified performance to 74.5% and is available to paid Claude users, via API, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud Vertex AI at the same pricing as Opus 4.

title: Tesla loses Autopilot wrongful-death verdict
summary: A Florida jury ordered Tesla to pay about $243 million to victims of a fatal 2019 crash involving an Autopilot-equipped Model S, finding the software defective. Tesla said the driver was solely at fault and vowed to appeal, while legal experts warned the verdict could complicate regulatory approval for its robotaxi expansion.

title: Little Caesars Launches Autonomous Robot Delivery via Uber Eats in LA
summary: Little Caesars, the nation's third-largest pizza chain, partnered with Serve Robotics to deliver HOT-N-READY pizza using autonomous sidewalk robots in the Los Angeles area, with orders placed through Uber Eats.

title: OpenAI releases first open-weight models since GPT-2
summary: OpenAI released gpt-oss-20b and gpt-oss-120b under Apache 2.0 license, its first open-weight models in six years, enabling free download, local execution, and customization without royalties.

title: Waymo & Uber Operate Driverless Robotaxi Service in Atlanta
summary: Since April 2024, Waymo and Uber have been operating driverless retrofitted Jaguar I-Pace robotaxis within a 65-square-mile area of Atlanta, Georgia. Atlanta is one of five U.S. cities currently offering the service, with expansion planned to seven cities by 2026.

title: Google releases Gemini 2.5 Deep Think publicly
summary: Google made Gemini 2.5 Deep Think, its first publicly available multi-agent model, available to Google AI Ultra subscribers on August 1, 2025. The model spawns multiple AI agents to tackle questions in parallel, and Google used a variation of it to score a gold medal at the International Mathematical Olympiad.

title: GenAI apps hit 1.7B downloads, double revenue in H1 2025
summary: Generative AI mobile apps reached 1.7 billion downloads in the first half of 2025 while doubling their revenue year-over-year, marking a concrete scale threshold for consumer AI adoption.

title: ADA Space Plans 12-Satellite AI Computing Constellation
summary: Chinese startup ADA Space unveiled plans on July 31, 2025 for a second-phase constellation of 12 AI computing satellites, codenamed Liangxi, with a combined computing power of 20 POPS, four times greater than the inaugural May 2025 batch. The announcement is part of its Star Compute program, which will ultimately comprise 2,800 supercomputer satellite systems.

title: Tesla Robotaxi Expands to Bay Area, California
summary: Tesla expanded its robotaxi service to the San Francisco Bay Area in July 2025, using safety staff in the driver's seat due to California regulations, and introduced per-mile dynamic pricing replacing earlier flat fees. Further rollouts are planned for Palo Alto, Brooklyn, Houston, Farmer's Branch, Tempe, Henderson, and multiple Florida cities.

title: Waymo announces Dallas robotaxi expansion for 2026
summary: Waymo announced plans to deploy robotaxis in Dallas in 2026, making it the second Texas city after Austin where the service will operate. Unlike Austin, where rides are ordered through Uber, Dallas will use Waymo's own service with Avis Budget Group managing the fleet.

title: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 runs Meta's Llama 4 Scout 109B locally on PC
summary: AMD announced that its Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 processor, paired with 128 GB RAM on Windows and the new Adrenalin Edition 25.8.1 WHQL driver, can now run Meta's Llama 4 Scout 109B (17B active) with full vision and MCP support. AMD says the model was previously only possible on datacenter-grade hardware, and is now available in thin and light PCs via its Variable Graphics Memory feature.

title: Microsoft Launches Copilot Mode in Edge Browser
summary: Microsoft launched an experimental, opt-in feature called Copilot Mode in its Edge browser, available free to Mac and PC users with Copilot access. The feature enables AI-assisted browsing including page-level assistance, multi-tab research, voice input, and agentic task handling such as booking appointments and drafting content.

title: Unitree R1 humanoid robot launches at $5,900 price floor
summary: Unitree Robotics launched the R1 humanoid robot at $5,900 (CNY 39,000), setting a new global price floor for full-size humanoid robots and marking the first time such a device has been marketed to consumers and developers at sub-$6,000 pricing.

title: OpenAI GPT-5 launch confirmed for early August 2025
summary: Multiple sources confirmed OpenAI will release GPT-5 in early August 2025, marking the first model to unify its GPT and 'o' reasoning series into Standard, Mini, and Nano variants.

title: Trump signs executive order barring 'woke' AI from federal contracts
summary: President Trump signed an executive order requiring AI companies that do business with the federal government to remove ideological agendas from their models, prohibiting federal agencies from contracting with technology companies whose AI chatbots exhibit partisan bias related to concepts such as diversity, equity and inclusion, critical race theory, and transgenderism.

title: NASA JPL Tests AI Dynamic Targeting on Orbit
summary: NASA/JPL's Dynamic Targeting system is being tested on Earth-observing satellites, enabling spacecraft to autonomously decide within seconds where to point instruments, avoiding cloud cover and prioritizing science targets in real time.

title: Alibaba releases Qwen3-Coder for AI agent development
summary: Alibaba launched Qwen3-Coder, a coding-focused open model that outperformed DeepSeek and Moonshot AI rivals in benchmark tests, targeting developer adoption of AI agents.

title: Google opens Veo 3 video model via Gemini API at $0.75/sec
summary: Google made its Veo 3 AI video generation model available to developers through the Gemini API, priced at $0.75 per second, supporting 720p resolution with integrated AI audio generation.

title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Agent combining Deep Research & Operator
summary: OpenAI released 'ChatGPT Agent,' the first product to unify ChatGPT, Deep Research, and Operator into a single autonomous agent capable of independent multi-step task execution. The launch marks OpenAI's first integrated agentic product for end users.

title: AWS Launches Amazon Bedrock Agent Core at NYC Summit
summary: At AWS Summit NYC 2025, Amazon unveiled Amazon Bedrock Agent Core, a suite of production-ready tools designed to bridge the gap between agentic AI proof-of-concepts and enterprise-grade deployments at scale.

title: UBTECH Walker S2 Gets World-First Autonomous Battery Swap System
summary: UBTECH unveiled the world's first hot-swappable autonomous power exchange system deployed on its Walker S2 industrial humanoid robot, enabling continuous operation without manual recharging downtime.

title: Claude Code Revenue Jumps 5.5x; Anthropic Adds Analytics
summary: Anthropic reported a 5.5x revenue surge for Claude Code and launched an enterprise analytics dashboard giving engineering leaders real-time productivity and ROI insights into AI coding usage.

title: ESA Φsat-2 begins science phase for AI Earth observation
summary: ESA's Φsat-2 miniature satellite completed commissioning in the second quarter of 2025 and entered its science phase, delivering onboard AI-processed Earth observation data including wildfire detection, ship tracking, and marine pollution identification. The mission also provides Level 1 data products to support AI application development and training.

title: Uber and Baidu Partner to Deploy Robotaxis in Asia and Middle East
summary: Uber and Baidu announced a partnership to deploy Baidu's Apollo Go autonomous robotaxi service on Uber's platform across cities in Asia and the Middle East.

title: US DoD awards up to $200M contract to xAI for Grok AI
summary: The US government announced a contract granting xAI up to $200 million to help modernize the Defense Department, one week after the 'MechaHitler' content controversy. xAI also launched 'Grok for Government,' with other federal agencies able to purchase its tools via the GSA schedule.

title: DoD Awards AI Contracts Worth Up to $200M Each to Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and xAI
summary: The US Department of Defense's Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office awarded contracts worth up to $200 million each to Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and xAI. Forrester describes the structure as a multi-vendor portfolio approach that lets the DoD draw on different providers' capabilities rather than committing to a single vendor.

title: AI Robot Autonomously Completes Gallbladder Surgery on Pig
summary: An AI surgical robot performed a full gallbladder removal on a dead pig without any human assistance, successfully completing 17 distinct tasks repeated 8 times each with a 100% success rate and self-correcting errors up to 6 times per task.

title: Grok AI Deployed in All Newly Delivered Tesla Vehicles
summary: Tesla updated its in-car software to include xAI's Grok chatbot, making it available in all new vehicles delivered on or after July 12 in the US at no additional subscription cost. Grok can answer questions but cannot interface with car functions such as navigation, volume, or climate control.

title: Moonshot AI launches Kimi K2 open-weight LLM
summary: Chinese startup Moonshot AI released Kimi K2, an open-source large language model built on a mixture-of-experts architecture with 1 trillion total parameters, designed to excel in knowledge, math, coding, and agentic tasks. The release reflects a broader industry trend toward open-source AI development, as Moonshot looks to maintain an edge against rivals such as DeepSeek.

title: Google releases MedGemma open-source medical AI model suite
summary: Google Research and DeepMind released MedGemma, a family of open-source AI models purpose-built for healthcare and life sciences, as part of its Health AI Developer Foundations initiative.

title: Tesla applies to test and operate Robotaxis in Phoenix, Arizona
summary: Tesla has applied to conduct autonomous vehicle testing and operations, with and without human safety drivers, in the Phoenix Metro area of Arizona, according to the Arizona Department of Transportation. A decision on the application is expected at the end of July, following Tesla's June pilot launch in Austin, Texas.

title: Google Gemini app gains image-to-video generation
summary: Google rolled out video generation from static images in the Gemini app for paid subscribers, expanding the consumer AI product's generative capabilities beyond text and image.

title: xAI Launches Grok 4 and Grok 4 Heavy with $300/mo SuperGrok Heavy Tier
summary: xAI released two new flagship models, Grok 4 and Grok 4 Heavy, alongside a $300/month 'SuperGrok Heavy' subscription plan. The company claims top benchmark performance on tests including Humanity's Last Exam and ARC-AGI-2, with Grok 4 Heavy described as a multi-agent version that spawns multiple agents to work on problems simultaneously.

title: Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 ships with Google Gemini built in
summary: Samsung announced the Galaxy Watch 8 ($350) and Galaxy Watch 8 Classic ($500), among the first devices to ship with Wear OS 6, which has Google Gemini built in. The assistant can be summoned by voice or a button, with preorders open and shipping beginning July 25.

title: Arbitrator rules Tesla breached FSD contract, orders refund
summary: A Washington state arbitrator ruled Tesla breached its Full Self-Driving contract with a Model Y owner, ordering a refund of US$10,600 plus costs, a first legal ruling that FSD failed to deliver as promised.

title: Waymo begins road trips to Philadelphia and NYC for AV mapping and testing
summary: Waymo launched 'road trips' to Philadelphia and New York City on July 7, 2025, sending human-driven vehicles equipped with its autonomous driving system to map and test the cities. The trips do not signal a commercial launch, as Waymo has not yet received approval to test autonomously in NYC and the city's regulations do not currently allow driverless deployment.

title: First AI self-monitoring satellite announced, 13-month build
summary: UC Davis and Proteus Space announced an AI-powered satellite built in 13 months that uses an onboard digital twin to monitor and predict its own power-system health in orbit. The satellite is set to launch in October 2025 from Vandenberg Space Force Base.

title: Tesla Halts Optimus Robot Procurement Amid Redesign
summary: Tesla informed suppliers of a roughly two-month halt on orders for its Optimus humanoid robot while design adjustments are completed, as the robot faces hardware challenges including overheating joints and low hand load capacity. SVP Milan Kovac, who led the program, has departed Tesla, with Ashok Elluswamy reportedly taking over responsibilities.

title: Google Veo 3 AI video model rolls out to 159 countries
summary: Google expanded its Veo 3 AI video generation model to Gemini Pro subscribers in 159 countries, enabling 8-second text-to-video clips with audio, marking the first global-scale deployment of a natively audio-capable video generation model.

title: Boston Dynamics Atlas to Deploy at Hyundai Georgia EV Plant in Oct
summary: Hyundai Motor plans to deploy Boston Dynamics' Atlas bipedal humanoid robot at its Georgia EV plant starting October 2025, marking Atlas's first industrial field trial ahead of full-scale commercialization.

title: Amazon Surpasses 1 Million Robots in Fulfillment Network
summary: Amazon has deployed more than one million robots across its fulfillment facilities, the most it has ever had and near the count of its roughly 1.56 million human workers. The company is also rolling out AI systems in its warehouses to improve inventory placement, demand forecasting, and robot efficiency, and says 75% of its global deliveries are now assisted by robotics.

title: Meta launches Superintelligence Labs division
summary: Meta formally launched Superintelligence Labs, a new AI division led by Alexandr Wang and Nat Friedman, consolidating its foundational model research and Llama development under a dedicated superintelligence-focused org.
